definition_zh: 许可；许可证；执照；正式批准；授权使用
definition_en: official permission to do something, the document that proves it, or the act of granting such permission
core_image: 权威递出的一把钥匙：门原本锁着，得到许可的人才能推开
scene: 市政厅窗口前，申请人接过盖了钢印的执照。The clerk handed over the business license, and the applicant put it in the same folder as her driving permit.
sceneCN: 这里 license 是「官方许可证」，也落在纸质证件这一层（第 1、2 个义项：官方许可；证明许可的证件）；句意：工作人员递过营业执照，申请人把它和驾驶证一起放进文件夹。图中可辨识物件：市政厅窗口、盖钢印的执照、文件夹、驾照；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 许可证；执照；许可；自由、放纵（古义/文学）
正式批准；给……发许可证；授权使用

collocations.zh: 经许可（授权生产或使用）
诗的破格；艺术上的自由处理

derivatives.zh: 已获许可的；持证的
被许可人；持证人
许可人；授权方
许可的颁发；执业许可制度

senses.title: Permission granted by an authority
senses.titleCN: 官方许可：权威解除禁令
senses.definition: official permission from a government or other authority to do something that is otherwise controlled or forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 政府或其他权威机构给予的正式许可，使原本受管制或被禁止的事可以做
senses.example: The company applied for a license to drill in the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司申请在海湾钻探的许可证。
senses.why: The Latin source is licere 'to be allowed', and its noun licentia meant 'freedom, permission'. The core scene is not a piece of paper but a gatekeeper lifting a ban, so the first sense is the permission itself; it can even be uncountable, as in work under license.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头是 licere“被允许”，其名词 licentia 意为“自由、许可”。核心画面不是一张纸，而是守门人解除禁令，所以第一义项是许可本身；它甚至可作不可数用法，如 work under license（经许可工作）。

senses.title: The document that carries the permission
senses.titleCN: 执照：把许可变成可携带的证件
senses.definition: an official card, certificate, or document that shows the holder has been given permission to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表明持有人已获准做某事的官方卡片、证书或文件
senses.example: He handed his driver's license to the officer at the checkpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 他在检查站把驾照递给了警官。
senses.why: Permission needs proof once it leaves the office. By metonymy the abstract grant becomes the object in your pocket: a driver's license, a business license, a hunting license. This is the countable, everyday sense and the one that takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 许可一旦离开办公室就需要凭证。借代让抽象的授予变成口袋里的实物：驾照、营业执照、狩猎证。这是可数、最日常的义项，也是能变复数的那个。

senses.title: A contract granting rights to use a work
senses.titleCN: 授权协议：允许他人使用作品或权利
senses.definition: a legal agreement under which the owner of a copyright, patent, or trademark allows another party to use it, usually for a fee
senses.definitionCN: 版权、专利或商标所有人允许另一方使用其权利的法律协议，通常收取费用
senses.example: The publisher bought a license to translate the novel into Chinese.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社买下了把这部小说译成中文的授权。
senses.why: Here licentia is narrowed from general permission to one specified right. The owner keeps ownership and hands over only a limited freedom, which is why a license is signed rather than sold: the thing granted is use, not title.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 licentia 从笼统许可收窄为一项特定权利。所有人保留所有权，只交出一部分有限自由，所以 license 是“签授权”而不是“卖断”：授予的是使用权，不是所有权。

senses.title: Literary liberty: freedom without restraint
senses.titleCN: 放纵的自由：不受约束的状态（古义/文学）
senses.definition: freedom to act as one pleases, especially when it goes beyond accepted limits; an older literary sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 想怎么做就怎么做的自由，尤指超出公认界限；该词较古老的文学义
senses.example: During the carnival, a spirit of license swept through the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 狂欢节期间，一种放纵的自由气息席卷街头。
senses.why: Latin licentia could mean both 'permission' and 'unrestrained freedom'. English kept the second branch: a license can be a state of liberty, not a document. Modern British usage usually spells this noun licence, while the verb remains license.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licentia 既可指“许可”，也可指“不受约束的自由”。英语保留了第二条分支：license 可以是自由状态而非文件。现代英式英语中该名词通常拼作 licence，动词仍作 license。

senses.title: To authorize an activity officially
senses.titleCN: 正式批准：官方放行某项活动
senses.definition: to give official permission for an activity, or to issue a permit to a person or business
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准某项活动，或向个人、企业发放许可证
senses.example: Only the city can license a new restaurant kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 只有市政府才能给新的餐馆厨房发许可证。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from about 1400 and was formed directly from the noun. The authority is the subject, the permitted activity is the object, and the act is a formal yes rather than a description of freedom.
senses.whyCN: 动词约在 1400 年出现，直接由名词转化而来。主语是权威机构，宾语是被批准的活动，这个动作是一个正式的“可以”，而不是对自由状态的描述。

senses.title: To grant the right to use intellectual property
senses.titleCN: 授权使用：把知识产权许可出去
senses.definition: to give a person or company legal permission to use a copyrighted work, invention, or brand
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人或公司使用受版权保护的作品、发明或品牌的法律许可
senses.example: The studio licensed the character for a series of toys.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室把这个角色的使用权授权给了一系列玩具。
senses.why: This is sense 3 as a verb. The owner stays the owner and lets someone else exploit the right; the object is a work or a right, not an activity, which separates it from license a restaurant in sense 5.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 3 义项的动词化。所有人仍是所有人，只允许别人利用这项权利；宾语是作品或权利，而不是活动，因此区别于第 5 义项的“给餐馆发证”。

senses.title: Social permission: a reason to speak or act
senses.titleCN: 理据性许可：有理由开口或行动
senses.definition: a fact, status, or circumstance that gives someone the freedom or justification to do something
senses.definitionCN: 某种事实、身份或情境给予某人做某事的自由或正当理由
senses.example: Twenty years of service gave her license to question the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年的服务经历给了她质疑这项计划的底气。
senses.why: No office is involved. The authority is experience, rank, or custom, and the phrase a license to do something treats that social standing as a grant. The word still performs the same act: it removes the risk of being thought out of line.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有发证机关。权威是经验、地位或惯例，而 a license to do something 这一说法把社会身份当成一种授予。这个词仍在做同一件事：消除“越界”的顾虑。

senses.title: Artistic license: the right to break the rules
senses.titleCN: 艺术破格：为效果而偏离事实或规则
senses.definition: the freedom that artists, writers, or performers claim to change facts, rules, or language in order to achieve an effect
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家、作家或表演者为达到效果而改变事实、规则或语言时自称的自由
senses.example: The film takes poetic license with the historical record.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影对历史记载做了诗意的破格处理。
senses.why: The fixed phrase poetic license shows the word at its most permissive: the permission comes from convention rather than an office, and the deviation is expected to serve the work rather than deceive the audience.
senses.whyCN: 固定短语 poetic license 展示了这个词最宽松的一面：许可来自惯例而不是机关，而这种偏离被期待是服务于作品，而不是欺骗观众。

senses.title: Fixed compounds and the licence/license spelling line
senses.titleCN: 固定搭配与拼写边界：license plate、licence/license
senses.definition: the noun as it survives in fixed compounds such as license plate, and the British and American rules that separate the noun licence from the verb license
senses.definitionCN: 名词在 license plate 等固定搭配中的用法，以及英式、美式把名词 licence 与动词 license 分开的拼写规则
senses.example: In British English the noun is licence and the verb is license; American English uses license for both.
senses.exampleCN: 英式英语中名词是 licence、动词是 license；美式英语两者都用 license。
senses.why: Compounds freeze the noun, which is why American license plate keeps the s. The spelling split follows the French-derived noun and the later English verb, standardized differently in Britain and America in the 18th and 19th centuries; in Britain the c marks the noun, the s marks the verb.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把名词形式固定下来，所以美式 license plate 保留 s。拼写分裂则源于法语来源的名词与后来英语派生的动词，18—19 世纪在英美分别被标准化成不同规则；英式用 c 标记名词、用 s 标记动词。

intro.en: License is a permission word, not a law word. Latin licere 'to be allowed, to be lawful' produced licentia 'freedom, permission', which Old French passed to English as licence. The modern split between the noun and the verb, and between British and American spelling, came much later.
intro.cn: license 是“许可”词，不是“法律”词。拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”产生名词 licentia“自由、许可”，古法语把 licence 传给英语。名词与动词的分工、以及英美拼写的差异，都是后来才形成的。

items.en: Latin licere 'to be allowed, to be lawful' gave the noun licentia 'freedom, permission, license' and the participle licitus 'allowed'. The core idea is permission granted, not a statute enacted.
items.cn: 拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”产生了名词 licentia“自由、许可、执照”和分词 licitus“获准的”。核心观念是“被授予许可”，而不是“制定法律”。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain. Licere is generally thought to go back to a PIE root *leik- 'to offer, bargain', also seen in Latin liceri 'to bid at auction'; this is a reconstruction, not a documented fact, and the intermediate steps are not certain.
items.cn: 更深的来源不确定。一般认为 licere 可追溯到原始印欧语词根 *leik-“出价、议价”，也见于拉丁语 liceri“拍卖出价”；这属于构拟，不是有文献确证的事实，中间环节并不确定。

items.en: Old French licence (12c.–13c.) meant 'freedom, liberty, permission' and came from Latin licentia. English borrowed the word rather than building it from parts.
items.cn: 古法语 licence（12—13 世纪）意为“自由、自主、许可”，来自拉丁语 licentia。英语是整词借入，而不是自己用词素拼出来的。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the late 14c. with both 'liberty, freedom' and 'formal permission from a superior'. The verb appears about 1400 as 'to give formal authority', and a 'give free rein' sense is recorded in the 1530s.
items.cn: 名词在 14 世纪晚期的英语中已有记录，兼有“自由、自主”和“上级的正式许可”两义。动词约 1400 年出现，意为“授予正式权限”；“放任、放开”义见于 16 世纪 30 年代。

items.en: The freedom branch stayed strong in the 16c.–17c., when licentious 'morally unrestrained' entered English from licentiosus. The permit branch gradually became the dominant everyday meaning, leaving the freedom branch as literary and archaic.
items.cn: “自由、放纵”这一支在 16—17 世纪仍很活跃，licentious“道德上无节制”就是此时从 licentiosus 进入英语的。此后“许可证”这一支逐渐成为日常主义，“自由”义退居文学与古旧用法。

items.en: License is not from Latin lex 'law' (genitive legis), which belongs to a different root and gives legal and legislate; the two words talk about rules but are not related. British English keeps licence for the noun and license for the verb; American English uses license for both. Compounds such as license plate, license fee and license holder keep the noun form.
items.cn: license 并非出自拉丁语 lex“法律”（属格 legis）；lex 属于另一个词根，衍生出 legal、legislate。两个词都谈规则，却不同源。英式英语名词用 licence、动词用 license；美式英语两者都用 license。license plate、license fee、license holder 等复合词则固定保留名词形式。

note.en: The look-alikes either belong to the Latin licere family or mark the noun/verb spelling line; the near synonyms each grant permission from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组要么属于拉丁语 licere 词族，要么标记名词与动词的拼写分界；第二组则从不同角度表达“准许”。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the noun only. British usage keeps licence for the permission or the document and license for the verb; American usage uses license for both.
entries.definitionCN: 只用于英式名词的拼写。英式用法中，表示许可或许可证的名词作 licence，动词作 license；美式则两者都用 license。

entries.definition: Lawful or permitted, from Latin licitus, the participle of licere. It is an adjective, not a permit, and has no verb use.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、获准的，来自拉丁语 licitus（licere 的分词）。它是形容词，不指证件，也没有动词用法。

entries.definition: Morally unrestrained, especially in sexual matters, from licentia 'freedom' plus -osus 'full of'. It carries only the excessive-liberty branch, never the permit branch.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上无节制的，尤指性方面，来自 licentia“自由”加 -osus“充满……的”。它只继承“过度自由”这一支，从不表示许可证。

entries.definition: To allow something, or an official document that allows it. It is the closest everyday synonym, though a permit is often a specific written allowance such as a parking permit, while a license usually certifies a professional or legal right.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事，或允许做某事的官方文件。它是最接近的日常同义词；但 permit 多指具体的书面允许（如停车证），而 license 常指对专业资格或法律权利的认证。

entries.definition: The act of allowing or the state of being allowed. It names the abstract grant only, never the card in your pocket, and it has no verb sense of issuing a license.
entries.definitionCN: 允许的行为或被允许的状态。它只指抽象的授予，不指口袋里的证件，也没有“发许可证”的动词义。

entries.definition: Official power or approval to act. It stresses the authority behind the grant rather than the paper or the freedom that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方权力或批准。它强调授予背后的权威，而不是证件本身或随之而来的自由。

entries.definition: A right granted by a company or government to sell goods or run a service under its name. It is a kind of license, but tied to a brand or a monopoly rather than to a single activity.
entries.definitionCN: 公司或政府授予的、以其名义销售商品或经营服务的权利。它是许可的一种，但绑定品牌或垄断经营权，而不是单项活动。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin licere 'to be allowed' plus -entia, with licit, illicit, licentious and leisure in the same Latin family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：拉丁语 licere“被允许”加 -entia，licit、illicit、licentious、leisure 都在同一个拉丁词族里。

normal.en: licere means 'to be allowed'. License is the allowed-ness itself, before it is ever a card in a wallet.
normal.cn: licere 意为“被允许”。license 首先就是这种“获准状态”，然后才变成钱包里的卡片。

normal.en: licentia covered both 'permission' and 'freedom'. The modern word still keeps the old freedom branch in literary use, as in a spirit of license.
normal.cn: licentia 兼有“许可”与“自由”两义。现代英语仍在文学语境里保留“自由”这一支，如 a spirit of license（放纵的气息）。

normal.en: The paper sense is a metonymy: the grant stands for the document that proves it, so a driver's license is both permission and proof.
normal.cn: 证件义是借代：授予本身代替了证明它的文件，所以 driver's license 既是许可也是凭证。

normal.en: Do not connect license to lex 'law'. Lex is about statutes and gives legal and legislate; licere is about being permitted, and the two only happen to talk about rules.
normal.cn: 不要把 license 连到 lex“法律”。lex 指成文法规，衍生出 legal、legislate；licere 指“被允许”，两者只是碰巧都谈规则。

normal.en: Spelling: British noun licence, British verb license; American both license. The c/s line marks word class, not a difference in meaning.
normal.cn: 拼写：英式名词 licence、动词 license；美式两者都写 license。c 与 s 这条线标记的是词性，不是意义差别。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door with a guard. License is the guard stepping aside — the permission itself, not the door and not the key.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门和一名守卫。license 是守卫让开的那一下——是许可本身，不是门，也不是钥匙。

abstract.en: Then the guard hands you a card so that other guards will step aside too. That card is the second sense, the license you carry.
abstract.cn: 然后守卫递给你一张卡，好让别的守卫也让开。那张卡就是第 2 义项，你随身携带的许可证。

abstract.en: When there is no guard at all, license becomes the freedom to act, which is why poets claim poetic license to break the rules on purpose.
abstract.cn: 当根本没有守卫时，license 就变成行动的自由；诗人正是据此主张 poetic license，故意打破规则。

examples.en: The university licenses its software to students at a reduced fee.
examples.cn: 这所大学以优惠价格把软件授权给学生使用。

examples.en: Her position gave her license to challenge the chair.
examples.cn: 她的职位给了她质疑主席的底气。

examples.en: In British English, licence is the noun and license is the verb.
examples.cn: 在英式英语中，licence 是名词，license 是动词。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来sense”——官方来了这份许可，事情才 sense 得通 → license 许可证；许可

root: 拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”→ 名词 licentia“许可、自由”。核心是“权威解除禁令、放行”，再由“许可”引申出证件、授权协议、自由放纵与艺术破格；与 lex“法律”并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of license, one movement: an authority lifts a ban, the permission becomes a document, then a limited right, then a social justification, and finally a freedom that needs no office at all.
sensesIntro.cn: license 的九个义项是一条线：权威解除禁令，许可变成证件，再收窄为有限权利，又转成社会层面的底气，最后成为无需发证机关的自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an authority hands over a key, and a door that was locked can now be opened.
core.cn: 核心意象：权威递出一把钥匙，原本锁着的门现在可以被推开。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: an authority lifts a ban, and the verb is that lifting done officially and out loud.
branches.cn: 权威：权威解除禁令，动词就是这一解除被正式、公开地做出。

branches.en: PAPER: permission becomes a document you carry, and compounds plus spelling freeze its noun form.
branches.cn: 纸面：许可变成随身携带的证件，而复合词与拼写规则又把名词形式固定下来。

branches.en: RIGHTS: a limited right is granted while ownership stays with the owner, in both the noun and the verb.
branches.cn: 权利：只授予有限使用权，所有权仍留给所有人；名词与动词都走这一支。

branches.en: FREEDOM: from unrestrained liberty to the artist's licensed deviation from fact and rule.
branches.cn: 自由：从不受约束的放纵，到艺术家获准偏离事实与规则。

branches.en: JUSTIFICATION: status, experience or custom acts as the authority that grants the permission.
branches.cn: 理据：地位、经验或惯例充当授予许可的“权威”。

intro.en: License is a borrowed Latin noun, not an English prefix-plus-root construction. English adds only ordinary suffixes such as -ed, -ee, -or and -ure; the endings -nce and -nse belong to the borrowed word itself.
intro.cn: license 是借入的拉丁名词，不是英语“前缀＋词根”的构造。英语只加 -ed、-ee、-or、-ure 这类普通后缀；-nce 与 -nse 的词尾属于借词本身。

latinIntro.en: Inside Latin, licere produced licentia and licitus, and those yielded English licence/license, licit, illicit and licentious. Leisure reaches English through Old French and is generally traced to the same licere.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语内部，licere 产生了 licentia 与 licitus，后者衍生出英语的 licence/license、licit、illicit、licentious。leisure 经古法语进入英语，一般也追溯到同一个 licere。

items.structure: license + -ed (past participle used as an adjective)
items.meaning: having official permission to do something
items.meaningCN: 已获官方许可的；持证的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: Only licensed drivers may use this road.
items.exampleCN: 只有持证司机才能使用这条路。

items.meaning: a person or company that has been given a license
items.meaningCN: 被许可人；持证人（-ee 表示接受者）
items.example: The licensee must renew the permit every year.
items.exampleCN: 被许可人必须每年续办许可证。

items.meaning: the party that grants a license to another party
items.meaningCN: 许可人；授权方（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The licensor keeps ownership of the trademark.
items.exampleCN: 许可人保留该商标的所有权。

items.meaning: the act or system of granting licenses, especially for a profession

definition_zh: 盖子；眼睑；限制；压制
definition_en: a removable cover for a container; also the fold of skin over the eye, or a check placed on something
core_image: 一只手捏住锅盖的提钮，把热气和味道扣在锅里
scene: 厨房里热气腾腾，锅里的汤咕嘟作响。She lifted the lid and let the steam escape.
sceneCN: 这里是「盖子」（第 1 个义项：容器的盖）；句意为她掀开锅盖，让蒸汽散出去。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、木质锅盖、灶火。

derivatives.zh: 由 eye 与 lid 复合而成，义为「眼皮；眼睑」

由 lid 加表示「具有」的后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带盖的」

senses.title: A cover for a container
senses.definition: a removable cover that fits over the top of a pot, box or other container
senses.definitionCN: 盖在锅、箱等容器顶部、可以取下的盖
senses.example: She lifted the lid of the pot and stirred the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她掀开锅盖，搅了搅汤。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the thing that closes a container; Old English hlid meant a covering that keeps what is inside in place.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指「把容器合上的东西」；古英语 hlid 就指覆盖物，作用是让里面的东西留在原处。

senses.title: Either fold of skin over the eye
senses.definition: one of the two movable folds of skin that close over the eye
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在眼球上、可以开合的两片皮肤之一
senses.example: His lids grew heavy as the film went on.
senses.exampleCN: 电影越放越久，他的眼皮越发沉重。
senses.why: Closing the eye is covering it, so the same word for a cover was extended to the fold that covers the eyeball.
senses.whyCN: 合眼就是把眼睛盖上，于是原本表示覆盖物的词，被用来指遮住眼球的那层皮。

senses.title: A check or limit on something
senses.definition: a limit that keeps an activity, price or piece of news under control
senses.definitionCN: 把某项活动、价格或消息控制住的界限
senses.example: The mayor promised to keep a lid on city spending.
senses.exampleCN: 市长承诺要管住市里的开支。
senses.why: A lid seals a container, and in speech the image becomes a seal on spending or news, so the word names control rather than a physical cover.
senses.whyCN: 盖子能把容器封住；用到言语里，被封住的对象变成开支或消息，于是这个词表示「控住」，而不是实物盖子。

intro.en: Lid is an Old English word for a cover, and its eye and restraint senses grow out of the same act of closing something.
intro.cn: lid 是古英语里表示覆盖物的词，眼睑与「压制」两个义项都从「把东西合上」这个动作长出来。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for a covering is believed to stand behind the Old English word, though its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为古英语词背后有一个表示覆盖物的原始日耳曼语名词，但更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Hlid named a cover for a container, and it could also name the covering of the eye.
items.cn: hlid 指容器的盖，也可以指眼睛上的那层覆盖。

items.en: Middle English kept lid for both the pot cover and the eyelid, and the spelling settled without the initial h.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lid 同时指锅盖与眼皮，拼写定型下来，词首的 h 不再写出。

items.en: The word spread from kitchens to workshops and became the ordinary noun for any removable cover.
items.cn: 这个词从厨房走进作坊，成为任何可取下盖子的常用名词。

items.en: Modern English adds a figurative restraint, so that a budget or a rumour can be sealed like a pot.
items.cn: 现代英语给它添上一层比喻性的「压制」，使预算或传闻也能像锅一样被封住。

note.cn: 第一组收同一「覆盖」意象或拼写相近的词；第二组收其他表示覆盖物的词。

normalIntro.en: Lid is a short Old English word for a cover, and its family keeps the picture of something closing over an opening.
normalIntro.cn: lid 是古英语里表示覆盖物的短词，它的同族词都保留「把开口合上」的画面。

normal.en: Old English hlid meant a cover, and the h simply dropped away in Middle English.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlid 意为覆盖物，到了中古英语，词首的 h 就消失了。

normal.en: Eyelid is eye plus lid: the lid that covers the eye.
normal.cn: eyelid 是 eye 加 lid，即盖住眼睛的那片「盖子」。

normal.en: Lidless drops the cover, so it means having no lid or no eyelids.
normal.cn: lidless 去掉盖子，所以表示没有盖子或没有眼皮。

normal.en: Keep a lid on turns a kitchen cover into a limit on money, noise or news.
normal.cn: keep a lid on 把厨房的盖子变成对钱、声音或消息的限制。

normal.en: A pot lid and a dustbin lid differ only in what they seal, not in the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 锅盖与垃圾桶盖不同的只是封住什么，词形本身不变。

abstract.en: Anything that can be opened has a lid, which is why the word moves so easily from pots to eyes to budgets.
abstract.cn: 凡是可以打开的东西都有盖子，所以这个词能轻易从锅移到眼睛，再移到预算。

abstract.en: A lid does not hide what is inside; it keeps it from escaping, and that is the link between cover and control.
abstract.cn: 盖子并不隐藏里面的东西，而是不让它跑出来，这正是「覆盖」与「控制」之间的连接。

abstract.en: The word is short and shut like the thing it names, a small sound that closes a container.
abstract.cn: 这个词又短又闭合，像它所指的东西，一个短短的音就把容器合上。

examples.en: She lifted the lid of the pot and stirred the soup.
examples.cn: 她掀开锅盖，搅了搅汤。

examples.en: His lids felt heavy after the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途开车之后，他的眼皮沉得厉害。

examples.en: The coach kept a lid on the team's excitement before the final.
examples.cn: 决赛前，教练压住了队员们的兴奋情绪。

definition_zh: 生命；一生；生活；活力
definition_en: the state of being alive; the period from birth to death; the way a person lives; and the energy that makes something lively
core_image: 一株小小的绿芽从土里顶出来，把光一点点变成生长
scene: 清晨的光刚落到窗台，病床上的老人睁开眼，握住女儿的手。The nurse stayed all night to save his life.
sceneCN: 这里是「生命、性命」（第 1 个义项：活着的状态）；句意为护士守了一整夜来救他的命。图中可辨识物件：病床、输液架、窗边的光。

derivatives.zh: 由 life 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无生命的；死气沉沉的」
由 life 与 long 复合而成，义为「终身的」
由 life 的词干加 -ly 构成，义为「活泼的；有生气的」

senses.title: The state of being alive
senses.definition: the state or condition of being alive, especially for a person, animal or plant
senses.definitionCN: 活着、尚未死亡的状态，尤指人、动物或植物
senses.example: The doctor worked fast because a life was at stake.
senses.exampleCN: 医生动作很快，因为有一条命悬在那里。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the bare fact of being alive, the opposite of death, and every later use grows from that fact.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指「活着」这个基本事实，与死亡相对，后来所有用法都从这一点生长出来。

senses.title: The span from birth to death
senses.definition: the period between birth and death, or the length of that period
senses.definitionCN: 从出生到死亡之间的整段时间，或其长度
senses.example: She spent her whole life in the same village.
senses.exampleCN: 她一辈子都住在同一个村子。
senses.why: Because being alive lasts a stretch of time, the word for life also measures that stretch, from the first breath to the last.
senses.whyCN: 因为活着会持续一段时间，表示生命的词也用来度量这一整段，从第一口气到最后一口。

senses.title: The way someone lives
senses.definition: the daily conditions, habits and activities that fill a person's existence
senses.definitionCN: 构成一个人日常存在的条件、习惯与活动
senses.example: City life suits him better than country life.
senses.exampleCN: 城市生活比乡村生活更适合他。
senses.why: Once life is a span of time, what fills that span also comes to be called life, so the word names habits and conditions rather than mere survival.
senses.whyCN: 一旦生命被看作一段时间，填满这段时间的内容也被叫作 life，于是这个词指习惯与环境，而不是仅仅活着。

senses.title: Vitality; liveliness
senses.definition: the energy or liveliness that makes a place, person or object feel alive
senses.definitionCN: 让场所、人或物显得有生气的能量与劲头
senses.example: Music brought the empty square back to life.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐让空荡的广场重新有了生气。
senses.why: The word for being alive can be moved onto things that are not alive, where it names the energy they seem to give off.
senses.whyCN: 表示「活着」的词可以移到没有生命的事物上，用来指它们散发出的那股劲。

intro.en: Life is an Old English word for being alive; it is related to the verb live and has no Latin word of the same meaning behind it.
intro.cn: life 是古英语中表示「活着」的词，与动词 live 同源，背后并没有哪个同义的拉丁词。

items.en: A reconstructed root often connected with remaining or continuing is proposed behind the Germanic family, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语族背后有个表示「留下、延续」的原始印欧语词根，但这一构拟并不确定。

items.en: The Germanic noun for life and the verb for living grew up side by side from the same stock.
items.cn: 日耳曼语里表示生命的名词，与表示活着的动词，是从同一来源一起长出来的。

items.en: Old English lif named the state of being alive and could also mean the course of a person's days.
items.cn: 古英语的 lif 指活着的状态，也可指一个人一生的历程。

items.en: Middle English extended life to the way people live and to the liveliness of things, while the plural lives took its present form.
items.cn: 中古英语把 life 扩展到生活方式与事物的生气，复数 lives 也定型下来。

items.en: Modern English uses life for biology, biography, daily existence and energy, and keeps live as the related verb and adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语用 life 指生理生命、生平、日常生活与活力，并保留 live 作为相关的动词与形容词。

note.en: The first group gathers the Germanic relatives of life and its compounds; the second gathers cooler abstract words for existing.
note.cn: 第一组收 life 的日耳曼语同族词与复合词；第二组收更冷静抽象的「存在」类词。

entries.definition: To be alive, or to spend one's life in a place; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 活着，或在一地生活；名词 life 背后的动词。

entries.definition: Without life; dead or dull.
entries.definitionCN: 没有生命的；死的或沉闷的。

entries.definition: Lasting for the whole of a person's life.
entries.definitionCN: 持续一辈子的；终身的。

entries.definition: Living, not dead; the same Germanic stock as life.
entries.definitionCN: 活着的、未死的；与 life 出自同一日耳曼语源。

entries.definition: The fact of being real or present, close to but cooler than life.
entries.definitionCN: 真实存在或在场的事实，比 life 更冷静、更抽象。

entries.definition: A living creature, or the state of existing.
entries.definitionCN: 活着的生物，或存在的状态。

entries.definition: The strength and energy that make something lively.
entries.definitionCN: 让事物有生气的力量与能量。

normalIntro.en: Life and live come from one Germanic stock, and the family keeps splitting that single fact into a noun, a verb and a quality.
normalIntro.cn: life 与 live 出自同一日耳曼语源，这一族词把「活着」这一件事分成名词、动词与性质。

normal.en: Life and live come from the same Germanic stock, one as a noun and one as a verb.
normal.cn: life 与 live 出自同一日耳曼语源，一个是名词，一个是动词。

normal.en: The plural is lives with a v, because the final f of life turns voiced between vowels.
normal.cn: 复数是 lives，带 v，因为 life 词尾的 f 在两个元音之间会浊化。

normal.en: Lifeless adds -less, the suffix for absence, so it means without life.
normal.cn: lifeless 加的是表示「没有」的后缀 -less，所以意为没有生命。

normal.en: Life expectancy literally asks how long a life is expected to last.
normal.cn: life expectancy 字面上问的就是一条命预计能持续多久。

normal.en: Come to life is used of things that are not alive, such as a party or a picture.
normal.cn: come to life 常用在本来没有生命的东西上，例如聚会或画像。

abstract.en: English uses one word for the fact of being alive, the years it lasts, and the way those years are filled, because all three are one experience seen at different lengths.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个词表示活着的事实、活着的年数以及这些年的过法，因为它们是同一段经验的不同尺度。

abstract.en: A life is both a line and a texture: it has length, and it also has a quality that can be dull or vivid.
abstract.cn: 一条命既是长度也是质感：它有长短，也有沉闷或鲜活的差别。

abstract.en: The word moves from biology to biography without blinking, which is why a person can lose a life and also live a life.
abstract.cn: 这个词从生理跨到生平毫不迟疑，所以人既可以失去一条命，也可以过一种生活。

examples.en: The doctor worked fast because a life was at stake.
examples.cn: 医生动作很快，因为有一条命悬着。

examples.en: He has lived in the same village all his life.
examples.cn: 他一辈子都住在同一个村子。

examples.en: Music brought the empty square back to life.
examples.cn: 音乐让空荡的广场重新有了生气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来福」——狗名来福，盼的就是性命平安、日子有生气；life 是生命、生活。

root: 古英语 lif（生命、活着）与动词 live 同源，一般认为其背后是日耳曼语族表示「存活、留下」的一组词；更深词源不确定，与拉丁语 vita 没有亲缘。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the fact of being alive; the senses then measure that fact as a span of years, as the way those years are lived, and as the energy they give off.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「活着」这一事实；义项随后把它量成一生的年数、看成这些年的过法，也看成它散发出的活力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small green shoot pushing up through soil and turning light into growth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株小绿芽从土里顶出来，把光一点点变成生长。

branches.en: a heartbeat returning on a monitor
branches.cn: 监护仪上重新出现的心跳

branches.en: one person's whole stretch of years in a single village
branches.cn: 一个人在同一村子里度过的全部年岁

branches.en: a first school morning and a grandparent's fixed routine
branches.cn: 孩子上学的第一个早晨与祖辈固定的日常

branches.en: two neighbours comparing city and country habits
branches.cn: 两个邻居比较城市与乡村的习惯

branches.en: a square waking up when the band starts
branches.cn: 乐队一响，广场就醒了过来

intro.en: One Germanic noun of being alive, its verb, two English endings and two compounds that turn life into a state, a lack and a span.
intro.cn: 一个表示活着的日耳曼名词、它的动词、两个英语词尾，以及两个把 life 变成状态、缺失与跨度的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vita means life, but it comes from a different root and is not a cognate of life.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命，但出自另一个词根，不是 life 的同族词。

definition_zh: 举起；抬起；提高；解除；电梯；便车
definition_en: to raise something to a higher place; to increase a level; to end a ban; and, as a noun, an elevator or a free ride
core_image: 两只手从下方托住重物，把它的重量抬离地面
scene: 楼道里的纸箱太沉，邻居伸手托住它的底部。He lifted the box onto the top shelf.
sceneCN: 这里是「举起、抬起」（第 1 个义项：把东西移到高处）；句意为他把这箱东西抬到最上层的架子上。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、货架、楼梯扶手。

derivatives.zh: 由 lift 加表示「人或物」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「举重者；升降装置」
由 lift 与 off 复合而成，义为「火箭等离地升空」
由 fork 与 lift 复合而成，义为「叉车」

senses.title: To raise something to a higher place
senses.definition: to move something upward from a lower position, usually with effort
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从较低处向上移动，通常要用些力气
senses.example: He lifted the box onto the top shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子抬到最上层的架子上。
senses.why: The Norse verb behind lift meant to raise, and the core picture is two hands taking a weight off the ground.
senses.whyCN: lift 背后的古诺尔斯语动词本义就是举起，核心画面是两只手把重量托离地面。

senses.title: To raise a level or amount
senses.definition: to increase the level, amount or value of something
senses.definitionCN: 提高某事物的水平、数量或价值
senses.example: The new bridge lifted property prices across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥抬高了河对岸的房价。
senses.why: Raising an object physically turns into raising a figure, because both move upward on an imagined scale.
senses.whyCN: 把东西举高这件事，转到数字上就成了把数字抬高，因为两者在想象的刻度上都是往上走。

senses.title: To cancel a ban or restriction
senses.definition: to end a rule, ban or order that was in force
senses.definitionCN: 结束正在实行的规定、禁令或命令
senses.example: The city lifted the night curfew last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天解除了夜间宵禁。
senses.why: A ban sits on people like a weight, so removing it is naturally described as lifting that weight off them.
senses.whyCN: 禁令像压在人们身上的重物，把它取消，自然就说成把这份重量挪开。

senses.title: An elevator
senses.definition: a machine that carries people up and down inside a building, the usual British word for an elevator
senses.definitionCN: 在楼内载人上下的机器，英式英语里常用的说法
senses.example: Take the lift to the fifth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 坐电梯到五楼。
senses.why: The noun names the device whose whole job is lifting, so the machine simply takes the name of the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词指专门负责举升的装置，于是这台机器直接取了动作的名字。

senses.title: A free ride in a vehicle
senses.definition: a ride given to someone in a car or other vehicle, usually without payment
senses.definitionCN: 让别人搭自己的车走一段，通常不收钱
senses.example: She gave me a lift to the station in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨天她顺路把我载到了车站。
senses.why: A ride lifts a person from one place to another, so an informal trip takes the same word as the upward movement.
senses.whyCN: 搭车就是把一个人从一处送到另一处，于是这段顺路的行程也用了表示上升的词。

intro.en: Lift arrived in English from Old Norse, where the verb for raising and the noun for air and height belonged together.
intro.cn: lift 从古诺尔斯语进入英语，在那里表示举起的动词与表示空气、高处的名词本是一族。

items.en: The verb lypta meant to raise or lift up, and it entered English during the Norse presence in the north of England.
items.cn: 动词 lypta 意为举起、抬升，在诺斯人活动于英格兰北部时进入英语。

items.en: The related noun lopt meant air or the sky, and it also named an upper room, which English keeps as loft.
items.cn: 同族名词 lopt 意为空气、天空，也指楼上的房间，英语保留为 loft。

items.en: Middle English lift worked as both verb and noun, covering the act of raising and the device that raises.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lift 兼作动词与名词，既指举起的动作，也指用来举升的装置。

items.en: The word took on figurative raising of prices, spirits and bans, while lift became the British word for an elevator.
items.cn: 这个词开始用于价格、情绪与禁令的抽象「抬高」，lift 也成为英式英语里「电梯」的说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps lift for raising, cancelling rules and giving rides, and uses lifting for the action itself.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 lift 表示举起、取消规定与顺路载人，并用 lifting 指举起这一动作。

note.en: The first group follows the Norse root through loft, aloft and the lift compounds; the second gathers other verbs for moving something upward.
note.cn: 第一组沿诺斯语词根收 loft、aloft 与 lift 的复合词；第二组收其他表示「往上移」的动词。

entries.definition: An upper room or a raised floor, from the same Norse word for air and height.
entries.definitionCN: 楼上的房间或架高的楼层，出自同一个表示空气与高处的诺斯词。

entries.definition: Up in the air; high above the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 在空中；高高在上。

entries.definition: A person or device that lifts.
entries.definitionCN: 举起东西的人或装置。

entries.definition: The moment a rocket or aircraft leaves the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 火箭或飞机离地的那一刻。

entries.definition: To move something to a higher position; the general verb for this action.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移到更高处；表达这一动作的通用动词。

entries.definition: To raise to a higher level, often in a technical or formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 提升到更高水平，常带技术或正式色彩。

entries.definition: To lift something heavy with ropes or a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 用绳索或机械把重物吊起。

normalIntro.en: Lift is a Norse verb of raising whose family keeps returning to height, and whose compounds keep returning to machines and movement.
normalIntro.cn: lift 是诺斯语中表示举起的动词，词族反复回到「高处」，复合词则反复回到机械与移动。

normal.en: Lift came from a Norse verb for raising, so its oldest job is to move weight upward.
normal.cn: lift 来自诺斯语中表示举起的动词，最老的本职就是把重量往上移。

normal.en: Loft and aloft belong to the same family, which is why all three suggest height.
normal.cn: loft 与 aloft 属于同一个词族，所以它们都带着「高处」的意思。

normal.en: Lifter adds -er, the doer suffix, so it names the person or machine that lifts.
normal.cn: lifter 加的是表示执行者的后缀 -er，指举起东西的人或机器。

normal.en: Lift a ban treats a rule as a weight, and cancelling it as taking that weight away.
normal.cn: lift a ban 把规定当成压着的重物，取消就是把这重量拿走。

normal.en: Give someone a lift uses the upward motion for a short ride to a farther place.
normal.cn: give someone a lift 用「向上移动」来表示顺路载人去更远一点的地方。

abstract.en: One word covers hands, prices, bans and elevators because each is a way of moving something up or off.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时覆盖双手、价格、禁令与电梯，因为它们都是把某物往上或往外移。

abstract.en: Lift is what you do to a weight, and it is also what a building does to people all day.
abstract.cn: lift 是你对重物做的动作，也是楼房整天对人做的事。

abstract.en: The word begins with touch and ends with permission, which shows how far one simple motion can travel.
abstract.cn: 这个词从触摸开始，到许可结束，可见一个简单的动作能走多远。

examples.en: He lifted the box onto the top shelf.
examples.cn: 他把箱子抬到最上层的架子上。

examples.en: The city lifted the night curfew last spring.
examples.cn: 这座城市去年春天解除了夜间宵禁。

examples.en: She gave me a lift to the station in the rain.
examples.cn: 下雨天她顺路把我载到了车站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「力扶特」——用力扶一把，特别能抬起来；lift 是举起。

root: 一般认为来自古诺尔斯语 lypta（举起），与 lopt（空气、高处，英语作 loft）同族；拉丁语 levare 只是意义相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is moving weight upward; the senses then split into raising numbers, removing rules, and the machines or rides that do the lifting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把重量往上移；义项随后分成抬高数字、解除规定，以及替人完成举升的机器与车程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands under a heavy box, taking its weight off the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手托住重箱的底部，把它的重量抬离地面。

branches.en: a box rising from floor to shelf
branches.cn: 箱子从地面升到架上

branches.en: a price line climbing after a new bridge opens
branches.cn: 新桥开通后上扬的房价曲线

branches.en: a curfew notice being taken down at night
branches.cn: 夜里被摘下的宵禁令告示

branches.en: a small metal box sliding up a shaft
branches.cn: 沿井道上升的小铁箱

branches.en: a wet passenger settling into a warm car
branches.cn: 淋湿的乘客坐进温暖的车里

intro.en: A Norse verb of raising, its noun for air and height, and the endings and compounds that turn the root into people, places and machines.
intro.cn: 一个表示举起的诺斯语动词、它表示空气与高处的名词，以及把词根变成人、地点与机器的词尾和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare means to raise and gives English lever and elevation, but it is not a cognate of lift.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levare 意为举起，英语的 lever 与 elevation 出自它，但它与 lift 并非同族。

definition_zh: 光；轻的；点燃
definition_en: brightness that lets us see, not heavy, or to set something burning
core_image: 窗边的书页被午后的光照得发亮，桌上的纸杯很轻
scene: 窗边的书页被午后的光照得发亮，桌上的纸杯很轻。Turn on the light, please.
sceneCN: 这里 light 是「光」（第 01 个义项）；句意是窗外的光把我弄醒了；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Brightness that lets us see
senses.definition: Brightness that lets us see
senses.definitionCN: 让人看见的明亮
senses.example: The light from the window woke me.
senses.exampleCN: 窗外的光把我弄醒了。
senses.why: Old English leoht named brightness; the word is Germanic and related to the idea of shining.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 leoht 指明亮；这个词属日耳曼语，与「发光」的概念相关。

senses.title: Not heavy
senses.definition: Not heavy
senses.definitionCN: 分量小
senses.example: The bag is light enough to carry.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包很轻，提得动。
senses.why: The adjective light comes from a different Old English word, leoht, meaning not heavy; the two words fell together in spelling.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 light 来自另一个古英语词 leoht，意为不重；两个词后来拼写合并。

senses.title: To set something burning
senses.definition: To set something burning
senses.definitionCN: 使某物烧起来
senses.example: She lit the candle.
senses.exampleCN: 她点燃了蜡烛。
senses.why: Because light can mean a flame, the verb came to mean setting something alight.
senses.whyCN: 因为 light 可以指火焰，动词就表示使某物烧起来。

intro.en: The history of light is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: light 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Leoht meant brightness.
items.cn: 古英语 leoht 指明亮。

items.en: Another leoht meant not heavy.
items.cn: 另一个 leoht 意为不重。

items.en: The spellings fell together.
items.cn: 两个词拼写合并。

items.en: Light as flame gave a verb.
items.cn: 光指火焰，引出动词。

items.en: Light covers brightness, weight and fire.
items.cn: 现代英语中它涵盖光、轻与点燃。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the word's real partners: its fixed phrase, its family, its recorded origin and its closest field.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子都建立在真实材料上：固定搭配、词族、可查的词源与最近的语义场。

normal.en: The fixed phrase 'turn on the light' gives the word one clear home.
normal.cn: 固定搭配「turn on the light」给了这个词一个清楚的落点。

normal.en: The family word 'lightly' shows how the meaning extends.
normal.cn: 词族里的「lightly」展示了词义如何向外延伸。

normal.en: Its recorded origin passes through OLD ENGLISH LEOHT and A SEPARATE LIGHT.
normal.cn: 可查的来源经过 OLD ENGLISH LEOHT 与 A SEPARATE LIGHT 两个阶段。

normal.cn: 同一语义场里还有「lamp」，回想时把两者放在一起比较。

normal.en: The form 'lighter' is what you will meet in running text.
normal.cn: 在连续文本里，你常遇到的形式是「lighter」。

abstract.en: Picture afternoon light brightening pages by the window, a paper cup light on the desk, then let the picture change size until it covers both the everyday object and the figurative use.
abstract.cn: 想象窗边的书页被午后的光照得发亮，桌上的纸杯很轻，再让画面变大变小，直到它同时罩住日常实物与比喻用法。

abstract.en: Place the word inside the scene given in this entry; what stays in memory is the picture, not the translation.
abstract.cn: 把 light 放进本词条给出的场景里；留在记忆里的是画面，不是翻译。

abstract.en: Link the word to one object you can point at, then to the idea that object lends to the other senses.
abstract.cn: 把 light 与一件能指认的具体事物挂钩，再挂到该事物借给其他义项的那层意思。

definition_en: with little force; in a small amount; without serious attention; or wearing little
core_image: 指尖像羽毛一样落在表面，几乎没有压下去
scene: 清晨的粥只撒了一小撮盐，味道刚刚好。The cook seasoned the soup lightly and let it simmer.
sceneCN: 这里是「少量地、轻微地」（第 2 个义项：用量或程度小）；句意为厨师只给汤里淡淡地调了味，然后让它小火慢炖。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、盐罐、木勺。

pos.zh: 轻轻地；少量地；轻率地；单薄地

senses.title: With little force
senses.definition: touching or moving something with very little force or weight
senses.definitionCN: 用很小的力气或分量去触碰、移动某物
senses.example: She touched the wet paint lightly with one finger.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个手指轻轻碰了碰没干的油漆。
senses.why: The adjective light means not heavy, and the -ly ending turns that quality into the manner of an action.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 light 意为「不重」，加上 -ly 词尾，就把这种性质变成动作的方式。

senses.title: In a small amount
senses.definition: using only a small amount of something such as salt or seasoning
senses.definitionCN: 只使用很少的量，例如盐或调味料
senses.example: The soup was lightly salted and tasted fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤只撒了少许盐，尝起来很清爽。
senses.why: A light hand puts on little, so the adverb measures quantity as well as force.
senses.whyCN: 下手轻就是放得少，所以这个副词不只量力气，也量数量。

senses.title: Without serious attention
senses.definition: treating something as unimportant or not worth serious thought
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当成不重要、不值得认真对待
senses.example: Such a warning should not be taken lightly.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的警告不该被当成耳旁风。
senses.why: Something taken light is given no weight, and in English weight stands for seriousness, so the adverb moves from the hand to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 被「轻」拿的东西没有被压上重量，而英语里重量代表认真，于是这个副词从手上滑到了心里。

senses.title: With little clothing or build
senses.definition: wearing few or thin clothes, or having a small and light body
senses.definitionCN: 穿得少或穿得薄，或身材小而轻
senses.example: He was lightly dressed for such a cold morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这么冷的早晨，他穿得实在太单薄。
senses.why: The sense of not heavy applies to clothes and bodies, so the adverb can describe how little a person wears or carries.
senses.whyCN: 「不重」的意思也能用在衣物与身体上，于是这个副词可以形容一个人穿得少、负担轻。

intro.en: Lightly is the adjective for little weight turned into an adverb; it is a Germanic word and not the same light that names brightness.
intro.cn: lightly 是表示「分量轻」的形容词变成的副词；它出自日耳曼语，与那个表示「明亮」的 light 并不是同一个词。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning light in weight and quick in movement is proposed behind this family, though the exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词族背后有个表示「分量轻、动作快」的原始印欧语词根，具体形式不确定。

items.en: The Germanic adjective meant light in weight and therefore easy to carry or bear.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的形容词意为分量轻，因此也指容易拿、容易承受。

items.en: Old English had two words of this shape: one meant not heavy, the other meant bright, and only the first is behind lightly.
items.cn: 古英语有两个同形词：一个意为不重，一个意为明亮；只有前一个才是 lightly 的来源。

items.en: The adverb ending -lice became -ly, and lightly kept the sense of a small weight or a gentle manner.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -lice 变成 -ly，lightly 保留了小重量与温和方式的意思。

items.en: Modern English also uses lightly for small amounts, for a lack of seriousness and for thin clothing.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 lightly 表示少量、不认真以及穿得单薄。

note.en: The first group collects the weight family and one word that merely looks similar; the second collects adverbs of gentle force or small degree.
note.cn: 第一组收表示「轻」的词族，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；第二组收表示轻柔力道或程度小的副词。

normalIntro.en: Lightly is the weight word plus an adverb ending, and it keeps the idea of a small load in the hand, on the tongue and in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: lightly 是表示重量的词加副词词尾，它在手上、在舌尖、在心里都保留「负担很小」的意思。

normal.en: Lightly is light plus -ly, so the adjective for not heavy becomes the adverb for a gentle action.
normal.cn: lightly 是 light 加 -ly，表示「不重」的形容词变成了表示动作轻柔的副词。

normal.en: English has two lights, one of weight and one of brightness, and lightly comes from the first.
normal.cn: 英语有两个 light，一个指重量，一个指亮度，lightly 来自前一个。

normal.en: Lightly salted means a light hand with the salt, not a bright taste.
normal.cn: lightly salted 指撒盐的手很轻，而不是味道明亮。

normal.en: To take something lightly is to give it no weight, which is why the phrase means not serious.

normal.en: Lightly dressed describes thin clothes, because weight and clothing share the same scale.
normal.cn: lightly dressed 形容衣服穿得薄，因为重量与衣装在同一个尺度上。

abstract.en: Lightness is both a fact about grams and a judgement about importance, and the adverb carries both.
abstract.cn: 轻既是一个关于克数的事实，也是一种关于重要性的判断，而这个副词两者都带着。

abstract.en: A light touch leaves the surface almost unchanged, which is why the word so often means care rather than weakness.
abstract.cn: 轻的触碰几乎不改变表面，所以这个词常表示细心，而不是无力。

abstract.en: One adverb moves from fingers to salt to warnings to clothes, and each step keeps the same small weight.
abstract.cn: 一个副词从指尖走到盐，再走到警告与衣服，每一步都保持同样的小小分量。

senses.title: The flash of atmospheric electricity
senses.definition: the bright flash produced when electrical charge in a cloud discharges through the air
senses.definitionCN: 云中电荷通过空气放电时产生的明亮闪光
senses.example: A single lightning strike split the old oak beside the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一次雷击把路旁的老橡树劈成两半。
senses.why: The noun names the visible event, the flash, rather than the invisible charge that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是可见的事件——那道闪光，而不是造成它的不可见电荷。

senses.title: A single discharge stroke
senses.definition: one return stroke of a discharge, which may repeat several times within a single flash
senses.definitionCN: 一次放电的回击，同一道闪光内可重复数次
senses.example: Instruments recorded four strokes inside one lightning flash.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器记录到一道闪电内包含四次回击。
senses.why: Physics needs to separate the flash we see from the strokes that compose it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学需要把肉眼所见的闪光与构成它的回击分开。

senses.title: A strike that hits something
senses.definition: a discharge that reaches the ground or an object and damages it
senses.definitionCN: 到达地面或某物体并造成损害的放电
senses.example: Lightning struck the church tower twice that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天，雷击了教堂塔楼两次。
senses.why: Once the flash touches something, the event becomes an impact with consequences.
senses.whyCN: 当闪光触到某物，事件就变成了一次有后果的撞击。

senses.title: Ball lightning
senses.definition: a rare glowing sphere reported to float for seconds after a strike
senses.definitionCN: 雷击后据报可漂浮数秒的罕见发光球体
senses.example: Witnesses described ball lightning drifting through the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 目击者描述球状闪电飘过厨房。
senses.why: The subtype keeps the base word and adds a shape, because the phenomenon is still classed as a discharge.
senses.whyCN: 这一下位类型保留原词并加上形状，因为该现象仍被归入放电。

senses.title: Extremely fast, as an attributive
senses.titleCN: 闪电般极快的（定语用法）
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean extremely quick, as in lightning speed or a lightning response
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前表示极快，如闪电般的速度或反应
senses.example: The agency mounted a lightning response to the outbreak.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构对疫情作出了闪电般的响应。
senses.why: Speed is read off the flash: the light appears and is gone before the eye can follow.
senses.whyCN: 速度是从闪光读出来的：光出现又消失，眼睛来不及跟上。

senses.title: A very brief visit or event
senses.titleCN: 极短暂的一次到访或事件
senses.definition: a short, intense visit or event that begins and ends almost at once
senses.definitionCN: 开始与结束几乎同时发生的短暂而强烈的到访或事件
senses.example: The minister made a lightning visit to the flooded town.
senses.exampleCN: 部长对受淹城镇做了一次闪电式访问。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows duration, not electricity: what matters is that there is almost no interval.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻借用的是时长而非电：要点在于几乎没有间隔。

senses.title: A sudden shock of insight or disaster
senses.titleCN: 突如其来的灵感或打击
senses.definition: a sudden, illuminating idea or a sudden destructive event likened to a flash
senses.definitionCN: 被比作闪光的突然顿悟，或突然的破坏性事件
senses.example: The solution came to her like lightning in the middle of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 答案在半夜像闪电一样击中了她。
senses.why: Both insight and catastrophe arrive without warning, which is the single feature the metaphor keeps.
senses.whyCN: 顿悟与灾祸都不打招呼就到，这正是该比喻保留的唯一特征。

senses.title: Sheet lightning without audible thunder
senses.titleCN: 只现光而听不到雷的片状闪电
senses.definition: a diffuse flash seen without a distinct channel, usually from a distant storm whose thunder is unheard
senses.definitionCN: 看不到清晰通道的弥散闪光，通常来自雷声已不可闻的远处风暴
senses.example: Heat lightning flickered along the southern horizon all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 整个傍晚，南边地平线上闪着无声的片状闪电。
senses.why: When the stroke is too far away for sound, only the illuminated cloud sheet remains visible.
senses.whyCN: 当放电太远、声音传不到时，剩下的只有被照亮的云幕。

intro.en: Lightning began as lightening, the verbal noun of lighten 'to flash', and lost its medial e in the modern spelling. The verb goes back to Old English lēoht 'light', a Germanic word whose Indo-European stock also produced Latin lux.
intro.cn: lightning 最初写作 lightening，是动词 lighten「发闪」的动名词，现代拼写中丢掉了中间的 e。该动词可溯至古英语 lēoht「光」，这一日耳曼词所属的印欧词干也产生了拉丁 lux。

items.en: Old English lēoht meant 'light, brightness' and also 'not heavy', a pair of senses still kept by the modern word light.
items.cn: 古英语 lēoht 既指「光、明亮」，也指「不重」，现代词 light 仍保留这两组意思。

items.en: In Middle English the flashing was called lightening, the -ing noun of the verb lighten 'to flash'; the modern spelling dropped the e.
items.cn: 中古英语把闪电现象称作 lightening，即动词 lighten「发闪」的 -ing 名词；现代拼写丢掉了那个 e。

items.en: German Leuchten 'to shine' and Dutch licht belong to the same Germanic stock, so the word is native rather than borrowed.
items.cn: 德语 Leuchten「发光」与荷兰语 licht 属同一日耳曼词干，因此该词是本族词而非借词。

items.en: Latin lux, lucis 'light' and lucere 'to shine' are distant cousins through Indo-European *leuk-, not ancestors of the English word.
items.cn: 拉丁 lux, lucis「光」与 lucere「发光」经印欧 *leuk- 与之远亲同源，并非英语词的祖先。

items.en: Only the weather sense survives in ordinary use; the verb lighten in the sense 'to flash' is now archaic.
items.cn: 日常使用中只剩天气义；动词 lighten 的「发闪」义现已古旧。

items.en: Source uncertain (spelling history): the loss of the medial e is usually explained by contraction in fast speech, but no single documented path is agreed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拼写史）：中间 e 的脱落通常用快速语流中的缩合解释，但没有公认的单一文献路径。

note.en: Group one holds the words most often confused with lightning by spelling; group two holds names for the same flash or for its parts.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写最易与本词混淆的词；第二组是同一道闪光或其组成部分的名称。

entries.definition: To make lighter or less heavy, or to brighten; despite the shared letters it is not the modern noun for the flash.
entries.definitionCN: 使更轻或更亮；尽管字形相近，它并不是现代指闪电的名词。

entries.definition: The equipment or design of lights in a room or on a stage; it has nothing to do with weather.
entries.definitionCN: 房间或舞台的灯具与布光；与天气无关。

entries.definition: A metal rod that carries a strike safely to earth; the compound keeps the base word unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 把雷击安全导入地面的金属杆；复合词保留原词形不变。

entries.definition: A shaft of lightning, or the act of striking; shorter and more concrete than the phenomenon itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一道闪电，或一次击中；比作为现象的闪电更短、更具体。

entries.definition: The instant of light, not the electrical process that lies behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 光出现的那一瞬，而非其背后的放电过程。

entries.definition: A lightning stroke imagined as a weapon, common in myth and older prose.
entries.definitionCN: 被想象成武器的雷击，多见于神话与旧体散文。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real source verb, the real cognates and the real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的来源动词、真实的同源词与真实的复合词。

normal.en: The word was once lightening, the -ing noun of the verb lighten 'to flash'.
normal.cn: 该词原本写作 lightening，即动词「发闪」的 -ing 名词。

normal.en: Latin lux and lucere are cousins through the same Indo-European stock, not ancestors.
normal.cn: 拉丁 lux 与 lucere 是同一印欧词干的远亲，而不是祖先。

normal.en: Compounds keep the base unchanged: lightning rod, lightning bolt, lightning strike.
normal.cn: 复合词保留原词形：避雷针、一道闪电、雷击。

normal.en: Resultative verb pattern: lightning struck the tower.

definition_zh: 很可能的；有希望的；合适的；可信的；大概；很可能地
definition_en: probable or expected; seeming suitable or promising; believable; and, as an adverb, probably
core_image: 云图上那片雨云正朝城市的方向缓缓压过来
scene: 清晨的广播里，播音员指着云图说今天午后有雨，出门的人顺手把伞塞进包里。The forecaster said it was likely to rain by noon, so she took an umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里是「很可能的」（第 1 个义项：表示某事有较大机会发生）；句意为预报员说中午前很可能下雨，于是她带上了伞。图中可辨识物件：云图、铺开的雨云带、塞进包里的折叠伞。

pos.zh: 很可能的；有希望的；合适的；可信的

senses.title: Probable or expected to happen
senses.titleCN: 很可能的；预期会发生的
senses.definition: having a high chance of happening or of being true
senses.definitionCN: 发生或属实的可能性很大
senses.example: It is likely to rain this evening.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚很可能下雨。
senses.why: The word grew out of like in the sense of having the same appearance, so something likely looks the way the expected thing looks, and that resemblance turns into probability.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从表示「长得像」的 like 长出来：一件很可能会发生的事，看起来正像预期中那件事的样子，于是「像」变成了「可能」。

senses.title: Seeming suitable or promising
senses.definition: seeming to be a good choice or to have a good chance of success
senses.definitionCN: 看起来是个好选择，或成功的机会很大
senses.example: She is the likeliest candidate for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 她是最有希望得到这个职位的人选。
senses.why: When a person looks the part, English calls that person likely, because the old sense of having the appearance of something turns into being promising.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人看起来就像那个角色，英语便说这人 likely，因为「具有某物的样子」这一旧义转成了「有希望」。

senses.title: Believable or plausible
senses.definition: seeming true or believable, often said of an excuse, an alibi or a story
senses.definitionCN: 听起来真实可信，常用于借口、不在场证明或说法
senses.example: That is a likely story, but I still do not believe it.
senses.exampleCN: 那说法倒像真的，可我还是不信。
senses.why: If something merely looks true, it can pass as true, and the ironic phrase a likely story shows exactly where appearance and credibility part company.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西只要看着像真的，就能冒充真的；反讽的「a likely story」正说明「像」与「可信」在哪儿分了家。

senses.title: Probably, as an adverb
senses.definition: used to say that something is probably true or will probably happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事大概属实或大概会发生
senses.example: They will likely agree to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们大概会同意这个方案。
senses.why: The adjective ending -ly already carried the sense of manner, so the same form slid into adverb use without taking a second suffix.
senses.whyCN: 形容词词尾 -ly 本就带「以……方式」的意味，所以同一形式直接滑入副词用法，不必再加一个后缀。

intro.en: Likely began as a word for looking like something, and only later came to mean probable.
intro.cn: likely 最初表示「看起来像某物」，后来才引申为「很可能」。

items.en: A root reconstructed as līka- is generally thought to mean body or form, and from it came words for being similar in appearance.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 līka-，意为「身体、形状」，由此产生表示「外观相似」的词。

items.en: Old English gelīc meant similar or alike, and the suffix -līc meant having the form of something.
items.cn: 古英语 gelīc 意为「相似的、相像的」，后缀 -līc 意为「具有……形状的」。

items.en: Old Norse líkligr, built from líkr and -ligr, meant likely or probable and strengthened the English word during the Norse period.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 líkligr 由 líkr（相像）与 -ligr 构成，意为「可能的、像样的」，在诺尔斯语影响时期强化了英语中的这个词。

items.en: Middle English used likli and likely for both a probable event and a suitable person.
items.cn: 中古英语用 likli、likely 同时表示「可能发生的事」与「合适的人」。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective and adds a fully accepted adverb use, especially in American writing.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词，并发展出被广泛接受的副词用法，尤其在美式书面语中。

normal.cn: likelihood 用 -hood 把形容词变成名词，与 childhood、neighbourhood 用的是同一个后缀。

normal.en: A likely candidate looks the part, and a likely story sounds true; in both cases the eye or ear decides before the mind.

abstract.en: Probability is appearance stretched over time: what resembles the usual outcome is expected to become it.
abstract.cn: 可能性就是把外观拉长时间：与常见结果相像的，就被预期会变成那个结果。

abstract.en: The same word serves a promise and a doubt, because a good appearance can raise either hope or suspicion.
