senses.title: Same manner: in the same way
senses.titleCN: 同样方式：照着同一套做法
senses.definition: in the same way or by the same method as someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 以与别人或别的事物相同的方式或方法
senses.example: She folded the map carefully, and he did likewise.
senses.exampleCN: 她仔细折好地图，他也照样做了。
senses.why: The word joins like, 'having the same form', to wise, 'manner'. The first sense is therefore the plain arithmetic of the compound: same form plus manner equals same way of doing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示“具有相同形体”的 like 与表示“方式”的 wise 合在一起。因此第一个义项就是这层构词关系的直接结果：相同形体加方式，等于相同的做法。

senses.title: Addition: the same is true of the second item
senses.definition: also or too, used when a second person or thing shares the same action, quality, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 也、同样，用于第二个人或物享有同一动作、性质或处境时
senses.example: The first proposal was too costly; the second was likewise rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 第一份提案成本太高；第二份也同样被否决了。
senses.why: Repeating an action in the same way easily becomes repeating the same verdict. The adverb slides from describing how something is done to asserting that the same predicate applies again.
senses.whyCN: 用同样的方式重复一个动作，很容易变成重复同一个结论。这个词于是从描述“怎么做”，滑向断定“同样的说法对第二项也成立”。

senses.title: Parallel clause marker: a matching statement follows
senses.titleCN: 平行句标记：引出结构对应的下一句
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, used to introduce a statement that runs parallel to the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，引出与上一句结构或逻辑平行的陈述
senses.example: The north wing needs repair. Likewise, the roof must be replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 北翼需要修缮。同样地，屋顶也必须更换。
senses.why: Once the adverb sits at the head of a clause, it stops modifying a single verb and starts organizing discourse: the next clause is offered as a second panel of the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词移到从句开头，它就不再修饰单个动词，而开始组织语篇：下一句被当作同一幅图的第二块面板呈现出来。

senses.title: Reciprocal reply: the same to you
senses.definition: in conversation, a short reply meaning 'the same to you' or 'I feel the same'
senses.definitionCN: 口语中简短回应，意为“你也一样”或“我也有同感”
senses.example: "Have a good trip." "Likewise."
senses.exampleCN: “旅途愉快。”“彼此彼此。”
senses.why: The comparison turns back on the speaker: the wish or feeling just received is returned to the sender. A whole clause is compressed into one adverb.
senses.whyCN: 比较的方向转回说话者：刚收到的祝愿或感受被原样送还给对方。整个从句被压缩成一个副词。

senses.title: Correspondence: standing in the same relation
senses.titleCN: 对应关系：处于相同的关系位置
senses.definition: in a comparison, showing that two things change or behave in a corresponding way
senses.definitionCN: 在比较中表示两件事以对应的方式变化或表现
senses.example: The two curves rise likewise during the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 两条曲线在第一季度以相同的方式上升。
senses.why: Here the shared element is not the action itself but the relation: each curve behaves toward its own baseline the way the other does toward its own. The same form is mapped onto two separate tracks.
senses.whyCN: 这里共享的不是动作本身，而是关系：每条曲线相对自己的基线如何变化，另一条也以同样方式相对自己的基线变化。相同的“形”被投射到两条独立的轨道上。

senses.title: Open extension: and similar things
senses.titleCN: 开放列举：以及诸如此类
senses.definition: in the phrase and likewise, used to extend a list to other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 用于 and likewise，把列举扩展到同类的其他事物
senses.example: The cupboard held flour, sugar, salt and likewise.
senses.exampleCN: 柜子里放着面粉、糖、盐以及诸如此类的东西。
senses.why: The same manner can widen from a single parallel case to an indefinite class: whatever else belongs to the same category is understood without being named.
senses.whyCN: “相同方式”可以从单个平行事例扩展到一整类：凡是属于同一范畴的东西，不必点名也自然被包括进来。

senses.title: Official parallel: the rule applies equally
senses.titleCN: 正式平行：规则同等适用于另一方
senses.definition: in formal or legal writing, used to apply the same rule, right, or duty to a second party
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或法律文本中，把同一规则、权利或义务同样施加于另一方
senses.example: The safety rules bind employees and likewise all contractors on site.
senses.exampleCN: 安全规定约束员工，也同样约束现场所有承包商。
senses.why: Official prose needs to bind two classes under one clause without repeating it. Likewise signals that the legal relation is copied exactly, which is why it is common in contracts and regulations.
senses.whyCN: 正式文本需要把两类主体绑进同一条款而不重复条文。likewise 表示这种法律关系被原样复制，因此常见于合同与规章。

senses.title: Usage boundary: affirmative parallels only
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：只接肯定性平行
senses.definition: a usage limit: likewise normally adds an affirmative parallel; in negative sentences English prefers either, neither, or nor
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：likewise 通常追加肯定性的平行项；否定句中英语更常用 either、neither 或 nor
senses.example: He did not sign the letter, and his partner did not either.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有在信上签字，他的搭档也没有。
senses.why: The word asserts that the same thing holds, not that the same thing fails to hold. Negative addition needs a negative polarity item, so 'did not likewise' sounds odd to most speakers.
senses.whyCN: 这个词断定“同样的事成立”，而不是“同样的事不成立”。否定追加需要否定极性词，因此“did not likewise”在多数母语者听来不自然。

senses.title: Register boundary: formal in casual agreement
senses.titleCN: 语体边界：日常附和时偏正式
senses.definition: a register limit: in informal speech, same here or me too is more natural than likewise, which can sound formal or stiff
senses.definitionCN: 语体限制：非正式口语中 same here 或 me too 比 likewise 更自然，后者可能显得正式或生硬
senses.example: "I'm starving." "Same here."
senses.exampleCN: “我饿坏了。”“我也是。”
senses.why: Because likewise began as a written-style parallel marker, its reciprocal use retains a polished edge. Friends usually choose a lighter phrase unless they are deliberately dry or humorous.
senses.whyCN: 由于 likewise 原本是书面风格的平行标记，它的回应用法仍带着修饰过的味道。朋友之间通常选更轻的说法，除非故意显得冷淡或幽默。

intro.en: Likewise is a Germanic compound made in English from like and wise. Dates are approximate, and the deepest Indo-European origin of like is not known.
intro.cn: likewise 是英语用 like 与 wise 构成的日耳曼语复合词。年代为大致估计；like 最深的印欧语来源并不确定。

items.en: Like goes back to Old English gelic 'similar, having the same form', a word built with the prefix ge- and the noun lic, which could mean 'body, form'.
items.cn: like 可追溯到古英语 gelic“相似的、具有相同形体的”，由前缀 ge- 与名词 lic 构成，后者可表示“身体、形体”。

items.en: The Germanic source is reconstructed as *galika-, literally 'having the same form', from *ga- 'together' plus *likam 'body, form'. The body-to-form shift is the interesting part of the story. The deeper PIE origin of *likam is source uncertain.
items.cn: 其日耳曼来源被重构为 *galika-，字面义“具有相同的形体”，由 *ga-“一起”加 *likam“身体、形体”构成。从“身体”到“形体”的转移是这段词源里值得注意的地方。*likam 更深的原始印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: Wise meaning 'manner, way, condition' is a separate Old English noun. It is related to witan 'to know', so the original sense is close to 'the way one knows or does something'.
items.cn: 表示“方式、方法、状况”的 wise 是另一个古英语名词，与 witan“知道”同源，因此其原义接近“一个人认知或做事的方式”。

items.en: The two words combine into the adverb likewise, first recorded in the late 14c. with the sense 'in like manner'. The written compound fixes a phrase that earlier appeared as like wise.
items.cn: 这两个词合成了副词 likewise，14 世纪晚期最早记录，义为“以同样的方式”。这个书面复合词凝固了早先写作 like wise 的短语。

items.en: Modern English keeps 'in the same way' and adds the discourse senses 'also' and 'moreover'. The adverb never inflects, and its reciprocal use in conversation is a later, familiar extension.
items.cn: 现代英语保留“以同样方式”，并发展出“也、此外”的语篇义。这个副词没有屈折变化；会话中的回应用法是较晚出现的、偏口语的延伸。

note.en: The first group shares the -wise shape or the like root; the second group approaches the same meaning from manner, degree, addition, and formal continuation.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -wise 词形或 like 词根；第二组从方式、程度、追加和正式递进四个角度靠近同一含义。

entries.definition: the state of being similar, or a picture that looks like someone. It keeps like but has no wise.
entries.definitionCN: 相似的状态，或看起来像某人的画像。它保留 like，但没有 wise。

entries.definition: in a different way, or in other respects. It uses the same -wise suffix but points away from sameness.
entries.definitionCN: 以不同的方式，或在其他方面。它使用同一个 -wise 后缀，却指向“不相同”。

entries.definition: in the direction in which a clock's hands move. It shows -wise as a productive suffix meaning 'in the manner or direction of'.
entries.definitionCN: 沿钟表指针移动的方向。它显示 -wise 是能产后缀，表示“以……的方式或方向”。

entries.definition: in a similar way. It is the closest synonym, but it compares two cases more openly and is less tied to a written parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 以相似的方式。它是最接近的同义词，但更 openly 比较两个事例，也不像 likewise 那样绑定书面平行结构。

entries.definition: to the same amount or degree. It measures quantity or rank, not the method by which something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 以相同的数量或程度。它衡量数量或等级，而不是做某事的方法。

entries.definition: in addition; too. It adds a further item but does not claim that the two items behave in the same manner.
entries.definitionCN: 此外；也。它追加另一项，但不声称两项以相同方式表现。

entries.definition: in addition to what has been said, used to introduce a further point. It is formal and sequential, not a claim of identical manner.
entries.definitionCN: 除已说内容之外，用于引出进一步论点。它正式且表递进，不是“方式相同”的断言。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real parts like and wise, real fixed phrases, and real relatives such as otherwise and clockwise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分 like 与 wise、真实固定短语，以及 otherwise、clockwise 等真实同族词。

normal.en: like means 'having the same form'; wise means 'manner'. Put them together and you get 'in the same manner'.
normal.cn: like 表示“具有相同形体”，wise 表示“方式”。合起来就是“以相同的方式”。

normal.en: The suffix -wise is still alive in otherwise, clockwise, and lengthwise, all meaning 'in the manner or direction of'.
normal.cn: 后缀 -wise 仍活在 otherwise、clockwise、lengthwise 中，都表示“以……的方式或方向”。

normal.en: Do likewise is a fixed phrase: whatever the first person did, the second repeats.
normal.cn: do likewise 是固定短语：第一个人怎么做，第二个人就照样做。

normal.en: As a one-word reply, Likewise means 'the same to you' and returns the wish you just received.
normal.cn: 作为一词回应，Likewise 意为“你也一样”，把刚收到的祝愿原样送还。

normal.en: And likewise at the end of a list means 'and other things of the same kind'.
normal.cn: and likewise 放在列举末尾，表示“以及同类的其他东西”。

abstract.en: Imagine one seal pressed twice: the second impression is not the first object, but it carries exactly the same shape.
abstract.cn: 想象同一枚印章压两次：第二个印痕不是第一个物体，却带着完全相同的形状。

abstract.en: A mirror placed beside an action: whatever the first body does, the second repeats in its own material.
abstract.cn: 在动作旁边立一面镜子：第一个身体做什么，第二个就在自己的材料里重复什么。

abstract.en: Two parallel tracks: they are separate roads, but every turn on one is matched by a turn on the other.
abstract.cn: 两条平行轨道：它们是各自独立的道路，但一条上的每次转弯，另一条都有对应的转弯。

examples.en: The first team simplified its forms, and the second team did likewise.
examples.cn: 第一组简化了表单，第二组也照样做了。

examples.en: The vaccine protects children; likewise, it reduces transmission in adults.
examples.cn: 疫苗保护儿童；同样地，它也减少成人的传播。

examples.en: "Thanks for your help." "Likewise."
examples.cn: “谢谢你的帮助。”“彼此彼此。”

dict_mnemonic.text: “来客歪姿”——来客摆出和别人一样歪的姿势 → likewise 同样地

root: 古英语 gelic“具有相同形体”+ wise“方式”，字面义“以相同的方式”；核心是“照着同一个形状再做一遍”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of likewise, all from one compound: like supplies the same shape, wise supplies the manner, and the pair is then extended to addition, discourse, reply, correspondence, open lists, official rules, and two usage limits.
sensesIntro.cn: likewise 的九个义项都出自同一个复合词：like 提供相同的形，wise 提供方式；这一对成分随后延伸到追加、语篇、回应、对应关系、开放列举、正式规则，以及两条用法边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same shape is carried over into a second act.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个形状被带进第二个行为里。

branches.en: MANNER AND CORRESPONDENCE: one method is copied, or two things occupy matching positions.
branches.cn: 方式与对应：一种做法被复制，或两件事占据相互对应的位置。

branches.en: PARALLEL APPLICATION: the same predicate is applied to a second item, a second clause, or a second legal party.
branches.cn: 平行适用：同一个说法被施加于第二项、第二句或第二个法律主体。

branches.en: RECIPROCAL REPLY: the comparison turns back and returns the wish to the speaker.
branches.cn: 回应：比较方向转回，把祝愿送还给说话者。

branches.en: OPEN CLASS: the same kind is left open, so the list can continue without naming every member.
branches.cn: 开放类别：同类范围保持开放，列举不必点出每一个成员。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: affirmative polarity and formal register limit where the adverb sounds natural.
branches.cn: 边界：肯定极性与正式语体限制了该副词听起来自然的范围。

intro.en: Likewise is a Germanic compound, not a Latin derivative. Like supplies the 'same form' and -wise is the noun 'manner' acting as the second element of a compound.
intro.cn: likewise 是日耳曼语复合词，不是拉丁语派生词。like 提供“相同形体”，-wise 则是充当复合词第二成分的名词“方式”。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate family here: like and wise are Germanic. The four entries below are the genuine Germanic relatives, including the still-productive -wise suffix and the wit family behind wise.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族词：like 与 wise 都是日耳曼语词。下面四条是真正的日耳曼同族词，包括仍有能产力的 -wise 后缀，以及 wise 背后与“知道”相关的 wit 词族。

items.meaningCN: 以同样的方式；也（like 表相同形体，-wise 表方式）
items.example: He nodded, and she did likewise.
items.exampleCN: 他点了点头，她也照样做了。

items.meaning: the quality of being similar; a portrait
items.meaningCN: 相似；相像；画像（-ness 构成状态或性质名词）
items.example: There is a strong likeness between the two brothers.

items.meaningCN: 讨人喜欢的；可爱的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: She is a likeable and patient teacher.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位讨人喜欢又有耐心的老师。

items.meaningCN: 喜爱；喜好（-ing 构成情感名词）
items.example: He has a liking for old maps.
The first half of the word is this old adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的前半就是这个古老的形容词。

items.structure: Old English wise 'manner', used as a suffix
items.meaning: in the manner of; as regards
items.example: The same suffix forms clockwise and lengthwise.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 clockwise 与 lengthwise。

items.example: The noun still survives inside the suffix.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词仍活在后缀里。

items.meaning: to compare one thing to another
items.example: The critic likened the novel to a long letter.
items.exampleCN: 评论家把这部小说比作一封长信。
这个俱乐部吸引志趣相投的读者。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 相似的；同样地（a- 加 like“形体”）

latinEntries.meaning: of the same kind or place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一类的；同一地方的（源自古英语 ilca“相同”）

latinEntries.meaning: way or manner, surviving mainly in compounds
latinEntries.meaningCN: 方式；方法（主要保留在复合词中）
才智；知道的能力（与 wise 同源）

definition_zh: 肢；四肢；大树枝；延伸部分；孤立无援的处境
definition_en: an arm, leg or wing; a large branch of a tree; and a risky or unsupported position, chiefly in the phrase out on a limb
core_image: 橡树粗壮的横枝朝一侧伸出，像一条展开的手臂
scene: 台风过后，院子里那棵老橡树被劈掉一大截横枝，断口露出浅色的木芯。The storm tore a heavy limb from the oak and left it lying across the path.
sceneCN: 这里是「大树枝」（第 2 个义项：从树干分出的大枝）；句意为暴风把橡树的一根粗枝劈下，横在路面上。图中可辨识物件：断枝、浅色木芯、湿漉的院子。

pos.zh: 肢；四肢；大树枝；延伸部分；孤立无援的处境

derivatives.zh: 由 limb 加 -ed 构成，义为「有……肢的」，多用于复合形容词
由 limb 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无肢的」
由 long 与 limbed 复合而成，义为「四肢修长的」

senses.title: An arm, leg or wing
senses.definition: a leg, arm or wing of a person or animal, especially one of the paired parts used for movement
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物的腿、臂或翼，尤指成对用于活动的部分
senses.example: He stretched his aching limbs after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行之后，他伸展酸痛的四肢。
senses.why: Old English lim named a jointed part of the body, and the word keeps that bodily core before it extends to other branching things.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lim 指身体上有关节的部分，这个词先守住身体这一核心，再扩展到别的「分出的部分」。

senses.title: A large branch of a tree
senses.definition: a large branch growing out from the trunk of a tree
senses.definitionCN: 从树干长出的粗大枝条
senses.example: The storm tore a heavy limb from the oak.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风把橡树的一根粗枝劈了下来。
senses.why: A branch leaves the trunk the way a limb leaves the body, so a word for a projecting part of a body was applied to a projecting part of a tree.
senses.whyCN: 树枝从树干分出，正如肢体从身体长出，于是这个指「身体外伸部分」的词也用到了树上。

senses.title: A vulnerable or isolated position
senses.titleCN: 孤立无援的处境；危险的境地
senses.definition: used in the phrase out on a limb to mean in a risky or unsupported position
senses.definitionCN: 用于 out on a limb 这一短语，表示身处危险或无人支持的境地
senses.example: By speaking first, she put herself out on a limb.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一个发言，把自己置于孤立无援的境地。
senses.why: A limb is what holds you up; to be out on one is to stand on a narrow branch far from the trunk, with nothing to hold on to.
senses.whyCN: 肢体本来是支撑身体的东西；而 out on a limb 就是跑到远离树干的窄枝上，身边没有可扶持的东西。

intro.en: Limb is an old Germanic word for a body part, and part of its history remains uncertain.
intro.cn: limb 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，指身体的一部分，它的历史有一部分并不清楚。

items.en: A form reconstructed as limu- is thought to have meant limb, but its links to other roots remain uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构形式 limu-，意为「肢体」，但它与其他词根的联系仍不确定。

items.en: Old English lim meant a limb or a jointed part of the body, and it could already be used of a branch.
items.cn: 古英语 lim 指肢体或身体上有关节的部分，而且已经可以用来指树枝。

items.en: Middle English wrote lim and limbe; the final b was added in spelling, probably by association with other words rather than by a change in sound.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 lim 与 limbe；词尾的 b 是拼写上添上去的，可能与别的词发生了联想，而不是读音变化。

items.en: Sixteenth-century printers fixed the spelling limb, and the b stayed even though it is never pronounced.
items.cn: 十六世纪的印刷者把拼写固定为 limb，这个 b 从不发音却被保留下来。

items.en: Modern English extends limb to tree branches, to the arms and legs of anatomy, and to the phrase out on a limb.
items.cn: 现代英语把 limb 扩展到树枝、解剖学上的四肢，以及 out on a limb 这一短语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on limb and a few close spellings; the near-meaning group collects the parts it can name.
note.cn: 形近组收由 limb 构成的词形和几个拼写相近的词；近义组收它可以指称的那些部位。

entries.definition: Having limbs of a stated kind, as in long-limbed.
entries.definitionCN: 有某种肢体的，如长肢的。

entries.definition: Without limbs of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何肢体的。

entries.definition: A place of waiting or neglect; the spelling is close, but the word comes from Latin limbus, meaning a border, so the two are not related.
entries.definitionCN: 等待或被人遗忘的境地；拼写相近，但这个词来自拉丁语 limbus（边界），两者不同源。

entries.definition: Supple and able to bend easily; its origin is uncertain and any link with limb is only suggested by the spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软、容易弯曲的；来源不确定，与 limb 的联系只是拼写上的暗示。

entries.definition: The upper limb from the shoulder to the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 从肩到手的上肢。

entries.definition: The lower limb used for standing and walking.
entries.definitionCN: 用于站立和行走的下肢。

entries.definition: A part growing out from the trunk of a tree.
entries.definitionCN: 从树干长出的部分。

entries.definition: A large branch of a tree, chiefly in literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 树的大枝，多见于文学语言。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and old, so its hooks come from the body, the tree and the idiom it feeds.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短而古老，所以记忆钩子来自身体、树木，以及它养出的那个习语。

normal.en: Old English lim meant a jointed body part, so the first picture is an arm or a leg, not a branch.
normal.cn: 古英语 lim 指有关节的身体部分，所以第一幅画面是手臂或腿，而不是树枝。

normal.en: The b in limb is silent and was added by printers; pronounce the word as lim and the spelling makes sense.
normal.cn: limb 里的 b 不发音，是印刷者添上去的；按 lim 来读，拼写就说得通。

normal.en: A branch is a limb of a tree because it leaves the trunk as an arm leaves the shoulder.
normal.cn: 树枝是树的 limb，因为它离开树干的方式，正如手臂离开肩膀。

normal.en: Out on a limb pictures someone standing on a narrow branch, far from any support.
normal.cn: out on a limb 画出一个人站在窄枝上，远离任何支撑。

normal.en: Limbed and limbless are built with -ed and -less, so they describe what a body or a doll has or lacks.
normal.cn: limbed 与 limbless 分别由 -ed、-less 构成，用来描述身体或人偶有或者没有肢体。

abstract.en: The body's branches and the tree's branches share one word because both reach out from a centre.
abstract.cn: 身体的分支与树的分支共用一个词，因为两者都从一个中心向外伸。

abstract.en: A limb is both a support and an exposure: what lets you stand can also leave you stranded.
abstract.cn: 肢体既是支撑也是暴露：让你站稳的东西，也能让你困在险处。

abstract.en: A silent letter is a small reminder that spelling often records the accidents of printers rather than the history of sound.
abstract.cn: 一个不发音的字母提醒人：拼写记下的常是印刷者的偶然选择，而不是声音的历史。

examples.en: He stretched his aching limbs after the long walk.
examples.cn: 长途步行之后，他伸展酸痛的四肢。

examples.en: The storm tore a heavy limb from the oak.
examples.cn: 暴风把橡树的一根粗枝劈了下来。

examples.en: She put herself out on a limb by speaking first.
examples.cn: 她第一个发言，把自己置于孤立无援的境地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林木」——林木伸出的大枝像一条手臂；limb 是肢体，也是大树枝。

root: 古英语 lim（肢体；身体有关节的部分），一般认为源自重构形式 limu-（肢体），与其他词根的联系不确定；词尾 b 为拼写添加；拉丁语 limbus（边界）只是形近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a part that reaches out from a main body; the senses divide into the limbs of a body, the branches of a tree, and the risky position of standing on a narrow branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「从主体伸出的部分」；义项由此分为身体肢体、树木大枝，以及站在窄枝上的危险处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick oak branch reaching out to one side like an opened arm.
core.cn: 核心意象：橡树粗壮的横枝朝一侧伸出，像一条展开的手臂。

branches.en: a swimmer stretching both arms
branches.cn: 游泳者伸开的双臂

branches.en: a broken bough across a path
branches.cn: 横在路上的断枝

branches.en: a voice speaking alone in a meeting
branches.cn: 会上独自开口的声音

branches.en: a shape reaching out from a centre
branches.cn: 从一个中心伸出的形状

branches.en: a figure standing on a thin branch
branches.cn: 站在细枝上的身影

intro.en: The word has no prefix, so the entries are its Germanic ancestors, its English forms and the suffixes it takes.
intro.cn: 这个词没有前缀，因此条目是它的日耳曼语先祖、英语词形，以及它接受的几个后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 限度；极限；界限；限制；限定；（口语）令人无法容忍的人或事
definition_en: the greatest amount or level allowed; a boundary; to keep something within a boundary; and, informally, an intolerable person or thing
core_image: 跑道尽头画着一条白线，越过它就算出界
scene: 操场边的公告牌写着每人每天只能领两瓶水，管理员站在桌后一瓶一瓶地数。The camp set a strict limit on drinking water during the hot week.
sceneCN: 这里是「限度、限额」（第 1 个义项：允许的最大数量）；句意为营地在炎热的一周里给饮用水定了严格限额。图中可辨识物件：公告牌、成排的水瓶、记账的纸单。

pos.zh: 限度；极限；界限；令人无法容忍的人或事

derivatives.zh: 由 limit 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「限制；局限」
由 limit 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无限制的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 limited 构成，义为「无限的；不受限制的」

senses.title: The greatest amount allowed
senses.definition: the largest amount, number or level that is allowed or possible
senses.definitionCN: 被允许或可能达到的最大数量、数目或程度
senses.example: There is a limit to how much I can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 我能搬的东西是有限度的。
senses.why: Latin limes was the path that marked the edge of a field, so a limit began as the line beyond which something stops being allowed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 limes 是标出田地边缘的小路，所以 limit 最初就是「越过就不再被允许」的那条线。

senses.title: A boundary between areas
senses.definition: a line or point marking the edge of an area, beyond which something else begins
senses.definitionCN: 标出某一区域边缘的线或点，越过之后就是别处
senses.example: The river forms the western limit of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河构成了老城的西界。
senses.why: The same boundary line can be drawn on a map as well as written into a rule, so the physical edge and the allowed amount share one word.
senses.whyCN: 同一条界线既能画在地图上，也能写进规章，所以实体边界与允许量共用一个词。

senses.title: To restrict something
senses.definition: to stop something from growing or going beyond a certain point
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某物继续增长或越过某个点
senses.example: The doctor limited his salt intake to one gram a day.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把他的盐摄入量限制在每天一克。
senses.why: Once a limit is a line, the verb is simply the act of holding things on the near side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 既然 limit 是一条线，动词就是「把事物挡在这条线的近侧」这个动作。

senses.title: An intolerable person or thing
senses.titleCN: 令人无法容忍的人或事（口语）
senses.definition: used in informal speech for a person or thing that is impossible to tolerate
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来指让人忍无可忍的人或事
senses.example: That child is the limit; he has emptied the whole box.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子真让人受不了，他把整盒都倒空了。
senses.why: When patience is used up, people say the behaviour has reached the limit, and the phrase then becomes a name for whoever caused it.
senses.whyCN: 耐心被耗尽时，人们说这种行为已经到了极限，这个说法于是直接用来指造成它的人。

intro.en: Limit comes straight from a Latin word for a boundary path, and it has kept the idea of a line ever since.
intro.cn: limit 直接来自一个表示「边界小路」的拉丁词，此后一直保留着「一条线」的意思。

items.en: Limes meant a boundary, a border, or the path that ran along the edge of a field.
items.cn: limes 意为边界、国界，也指标出田地边缘的那条小路。

items.en: The genitive limitis gave the stem limit-, which English kept in every form of the word.
items.cn: 属格 limitis 给出词干 limit-，英语把这个词干保留在这个词的各种形式里。

items.en: The verb limitare meant to mark out a boundary or to set bounds, and it supplied the idea of restricting.
items.cn: 动词 limitare 意为标出边界、设定范围，提供了「加以限制」这一层意思。

items.en: Middle English took limit from French and used it for a boundary or a fixed extent.
items.cn: 中古英语经法语引入 limit，用来指边界或固定的范围。

items.en: Modern English adds the everyday sense of a maximum amount and the informal sense of an intolerable person.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「最大数量」的日常义项，以及「无法容忍的人」这一口语义项。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin boundary stem; the near-meaning group gathers other words for edges and restrictions.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示边界的拉丁词干展开；近义组收表示界线与限制的其他词。

entries.definition: A rule or condition that restricts what is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 限制可能范围的规则或条件。

entries.definition: Having no limit at all.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何限度的。

entries.definition: Not restricted by any limit.
entries.definitionCN: 不受任何限制的。

entries.definition: To mark the boundary of something.
entries.definitionCN: 标出某物的边界。

entries.definition: A line that marks where an area ends.
entries.definitionCN: 标出区域终点的线。

entries.definition: The point at which something begins or stops.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物开始或停止的那个点。

entries.definition: An upper limit set on an amount, especially money.
entries.definitionCN: 对数量尤其是金额设定的上限。

entries.definition: A rule that limits what people may do.
entries.definitionCN: 限制人们行为的规定。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin boundary line, so every hook draws a line and then stands on one side of it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一条拉丁语的边界线，所以每条钩子都先画线，再站到线的一侧。

normal.en: Limes was a path along the edge of a field, so every limit is first a line drawn on the ground.
normal.cn: limes 是沿着田地边缘的小路，所以每个 limit 首先都是画在地上的一条线。

normal.en: The stem limit- never changes: limits, limited and limiting all keep it intact.
normal.cn: 词干 limit- 始终不变：limits、limited、limiting 都完整保留它。

normal.en: Speed limit, time limit and age limit all name the number placed on the far side of the line.
normal.cn: speed limit、time limit、age limit 都是把线另一侧的那个数字说出来。

normal.en: To limit something is to make the line do work, holding growth on the near side.
normal.cn: to limit 某物就是让这条线起作用，把增长挡在近侧。

normal.en: Limitation and limitless take opposite suffixes, -ation and -less, from the same stem.
normal.cn: limitation 与 limitless 在同一词干上加了相反的后缀 -ation 与 -less。

abstract.en: A boundary is useful only because something lies on both sides of it: the word carries the outside with it.
abstract.cn: 边界之所以有用，是因为线两边都有东西：这个词把「外面」也一起带着。

abstract.en: To set a limit is an act of trust in advance, a way of saying how far a relationship will go.
abstract.cn: 设定限度是一种事先的信任，是在说明这层关系能走多远。

abstract.en: When patience runs out, the same word that measured things turns and measures a person.
abstract.cn: 当耐心耗尽，这个原本量事物的词就转过身来量人。

examples.en: There is a limit to how much I can carry.
examples.cn: 我能搬的东西是有限度的。

examples.en: The doctor limited his salt intake to one gram a day.
examples.cn: 医生把他的盐摄入量限制在每天一克。

examples.en: The speed limit on this road is forty.
examples.cn: 这条路的限速是四十。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厘米特」——绳子只到厘米特那么长，再多一厘米就超过限度；limit 是限度。

root: 拉丁语 limes（边界、田边小路），属格 limitis 给出词干 limit-；晚期拉丁语 limitare（划定界限）→ 法语 limite → 英语 limit；同族词多与边界、限制有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a boundary line; the senses divide into the maximum allowed, the geographical edge, the act of restricting, and the point where tolerance runs out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一条界线」；义项由此分为允许的最大量、地理边界、划线限制的动作，以及耐心到顶时对人的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line painted at the end of a running track.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道尽头画着一条白线，越过它就算出界。

branches.en: a notice board listing two bottles a day
branches.cn: 写着每天两瓶的公告牌

branches.en: a river marking the edge of a town
branches.cn: 标出城镇边缘的一条河

branches.en: a doctor writing a daily maximum
branches.cn: 医生写下的每日上限

branches.en: an empty box and a tired parent
branches.cn: 空盒子和疲惫的家长

branches.en: a white line at the end of a track
branches.cn: 跑道尽头的白线

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun of boundary, its genitive stem and a Late Latin verb of marking bounds.
intro.cn: 这个词依托表示边界的拉丁名词、它的属格词干，以及一个表示划界的晚期拉丁语动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

latinEntries.meaning: to mark a boundary, to restrict

definition_zh: 限制；限度；局限；不足之处；（法律）诉讼时效；责任限额；权利或地产的限定
definition_en: a rule or condition that limits something, and a weakness or shortcoming that a method or person cannot pass
core_image: 一条画在路面上的白线，把可以走的范围圈在里面，圈外一步也不许越
scene: 论文末尾专门用一节说明样本太小、只覆盖一所学校，提醒读者结论不能推得太远。Every study states its limitations so that readers know how far the findings can travel.
sceneCN: 这里指研究自身的不足之处（第 4 个义项：局限、不足）；句意为每项研究都要说明自己的局限，读者才知道结论能走多远。场景图取象：路面上一条白线把可行范围圈住；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 限制；限度（可数或不可数）
局限；不足之处（多用复数）

derivatives.zh: 界限；限制（由拉丁语「边界」一词直接借入，兼指界线与设界之举）
有限的；受限制的（动词过去分词转形容词，指数量或范围受约束）
无限的；无边的（加表示「没有」的形容词后缀）
划定界限；划界（加表示「去除、划分」的前缀，指把边界明确画出）
限制性的（现在分词转形容词，指起约束作用）
无限的；不受限制的（加否定前缀，指没有设上限）

senses.title: The act of limiting
senses.definition: the act of keeping something within bounds, or the state of being kept within them
senses.definitionCN: 把某物保持在范围之内的动作，或受此约束的状态
senses.example: The limitation of outdoor gatherings began in October.
senses.exampleCN: 户外聚集的限制从十月开始。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to bound, so the act of drawing the line is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自意为「划界」的拉丁动词，画线这个动作是最古老的义项。

senses.title: A rule that restricts
senses.definition: a rule, condition or cap that restricts what may be done, used or claimed
senses.definitionCN: 限制可以做什么、用多少或主张什么的规则、条件或上限
senses.example: The contract places a limitation on how many copies may be made.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对可以制作多少份副本设了限制。
senses.why: Once a line is drawn, people need it written down, and the written line is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 线一旦画出，人们就需要把它写下来，写下来的线就是这一义项。

senses.title: A cap on money or time
senses.definition: a fixed upper amount of money, time or resources allowed for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某项用途所允许的金钱、时间或资源的固定上限
senses.example: There is a strict limitation on the daily water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 每日供水量有严格上限。
senses.why: Budgets and clocks are the most concrete boundaries, so the word settles there first.
senses.whyCN: 预算与时钟是最具体的边界，这个词先在这里落脚。

senses.title: A weakness of a method
senses.definition: a shortcoming in a study, method or tool that limits what its results can support
senses.definitionCN: 研究、方法或工具中的不足，限制了其结果能支撑的结论
senses.example: Every study states its limitations so that readers know how far the findings can travel.
senses.exampleCN: 每项研究都要说明自己的局限，读者才知道结论能走多远。
senses.why: Science uses the plural to admit what a design cannot see, and that candour is part of the method.
senses.whyCN: 科学用复数形式承认设计看不到的东西，这种坦白本身就是方法的一部分。

senses.title: The statute of limitations
senses.definition: the legal time limit within which a claim must be brought before it is barred
senses.definitionCN: 必须在期限之内提起诉讼、逾期即丧失胜诉权的法定时限
senses.example: The claim was dismissed because the limitation had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 由于时效已过，这项请求被驳回。
senses.why: Law puts a clock on every right, and the time limit is named after the limiting itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律给每项权利都装上时钟，这个时限就以「限制」这个动作为名。

senses.title: A cap on liability
senses.definition: a contractual maximum on the amount one party must pay for loss or damage
senses.definitionCN: 合同规定的、一方对损失或损害必须支付的最高金额
senses.example: The insurer accepted a limitation of liability of two million.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人接受了二百万的责任限额。
senses.why: Risk is made bearable by naming the worst number in advance, and the clause is named after that cap.
senses.whyCN: 事先把最坏的数字写出来，风险才可承受，这条款便以那个上限命名。

senses.title: A limit on an estate or right
senses.definition: a legal restriction on how long an estate or right may last or how it may pass
senses.definitionCN: 对某项地产或权利存续时间或转让方式的法定限定
senses.example: The deed carried a limitation on the sale of the land.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据对土地的出售作了限定。
senses.why: Property law inherited the Roman boundary word and uses it for estates cut down to a fixed term.
senses.whyCN: 财产法继承了罗马的边界词，用它指被限定为固定期限的产权。

senses.title: A caveat in an argument
senses.definition: a qualification attached to a claim so that it is not taken too broadly
senses.definitionCN: 附加在主张之上的限定条件，使其不被过度推广
senses.example: He added a limitation: the rule holds only for small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 他加了一个限定：这条规则只适用于小公司。
senses.why: A wise claim fences its own reach, and the fence is called a limitation.
senses.whyCN: 审慎的主张会替自己围出边界，这道围栏就叫限定。

senses.title: A boundary in space
senses.definition: an outer boundary or edge, the oldest physical sense of the root
senses.definitionCN: 外部的边界或边缘，是这个词根最古老的具体含义
senses.example: The limitation of the old city wall still shows on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 旧城墙的边界在地图上仍看得出来。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a frontier between fields, and every later sense is a descendant of that ditch.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本指田地之间的地界，后来所有义项都是那条沟的后代。

intro.en: Limitation comes from Latin limitare 'to bound', from limes, 'boundary, frontier'. The line of descent is clear; the exact date of the English noun is uncertain.
intro.cn: limitation 来自拉丁语 limitare「划界」，出自 limes「边界、前线」。词源线索清楚，这个英语名词出现的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Limes meant a boundary line, a frontier between fields or between provinces of the empire.
items.cn: limes 意为边界线，是田地之间或帝国行省之间的分界线。

items.en: The verb limitare meant to mark a boundary and, by extension, to keep something within it.
items.cn: 动词 limitare 意为标出边界，引申为把某物留在边界之内。

items.en: Limitio and limitatio named the marking of a bound, a word of surveyors and lawyers.
items.cn: limitio 与 limitatio 指划定边界，是测量员与法律人的用语。

items.en: The noun entered English in the fifteenth century through legal and scholarly French; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪经由法律与学术法语进入英语；确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English split the word two ways: the limitations of a study, and the limitation of liability in a contract.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分成两支：研究的局限，以及合同中的责任限额。

items.en: The statute of limitations gave the word a clock, naming the period beyond which a right cannot be pursued.
items.cn: 诉讼时效法规给这个词装上了时钟，指超过之后权利便无法追索的期间。

note.en: The first group shares the boundary root or looks close; the second group holds the words that often stand in for limitation in argument and in law.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「边界」词根，或字形相近；第二组是论证与法律中常替代「限制、局限」的词。

entries.definition: The plain noun and verb for a boundary or a cap.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的边界或上限名词，也可作动词。

entries.definition: Restricted in amount or scope, the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或范围上受限制的形容词。

entries.definition: The drawing of a boundary, especially between states or fields.
entries.definitionCN: 划定边界，尤指国界或领域之间。

entries.definition: To remove something; it looks like the same family but comes from limen, a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 清除某物；看似同族，其实出自意为「门槛」的 limen。

entries.definition: Occupying a threshold or in-between state, from limen rather than limes.
entries.definitionCN: 处于门槛或过渡状态，出自 limen 而非 limes。

entries.definition: A rule that prevents something, often imposed by authority.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事的规则，通常由权威施加。

entries.definition: A factor that forces a choice, close to limitation in research writing.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使作出选择的因素，在研究写作中接近「局限」。

entries.definition: A failure to reach a standard, the plain word for a weakness.
entries.definitionCN: 未能达到标准，是最朴素的「缺点」说法。

entries.definition: A disadvantage that makes something less attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物吸引力下降的不利之处。

entries.definition: A warning or condition attached to a claim or permission.
entries.definitionCN: 附在主张或许可之上的警告或条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real frontier word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「边界」词、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Limes meant the frontier of the empire, so a limitation is a line drawn at the edge of what is allowed.
normal.cn: limes 指帝国的前线，限制就是画在允许范围边缘的一条线。

normal.en: The family runs limit, limited, limitless and delimitation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 limit、limited、limitless 与 delimitation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: limitations of the study, time limitation, limitation of liability.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：研究的局限、时间限制、责任限额。

normal.en: In law the plural has a life of its own: the statute of limitations.
normal.cn: 在法律里复数形式自成一体：诉讼时效。

normal.en: Eliminate and liminal are false friends; they come from limen, a threshold.
normal.cn: eliminate 与 liminal 是假朋友，它们出自意为门槛的 limen。

abstract.en: A limitation honestly stated is a gift to the reader, not a weakness of the writer.
abstract.cn: 老实说出的局限是给读者的礼物，而不是作者的无能。

abstract.en: Every boundary that keeps something in also keeps something out.
abstract.cn: 每道把东西圈进来的边界，也把另一些东西关在外面。

abstract.en: The line that protects also instructs; it tells you where the work begins.
abstract.cn: 起保护作用的线同时在指路，它告诉你工作从哪里开始。

examples.en: The report lists three limitations of its own method.
examples.cn: 报告列出自身方法的三处局限。

examples.en: A limitation on imports raised the price of steel.
examples.cn: 进口限制抬高了钢材价格。

examples.en: The suit was filed within the limitation period.
examples.cn: 诉讼是在时效期间内提起的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「利米泰申」——地上画一条白线，线外不许走：限制、局限

root: 拉丁语 limitare「划界」← limes「边界、前线」；经法律与学术法语于十五世纪进入英语。同族有 limit、limited、delimitation；eliminate 与 liminal 出自 limen「门槛」，属形近不同源。名词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all descend from one boundary: the act of bounding, a restricting rule, a cap on money or time, a weakness of method, the statute of limitations, a liability cap, a limit on an estate, a caveat in argument, and a boundary in space.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都出自同一条边界：划界之举、限制性规定、金额或时间的上限、方法的局限、诉讼时效、责任限额、对地产或权利的限定、论证中的保留，以及空间上的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line painted across a road, with everything beyond it out of bounds.
core.cn: 核心意象：路面上画着一条白线，线外一切都不得越过。

branches.en: THE LINE ITSELF: a frontier drawn in space, and the act of drawing it.
branches.cn: 线本身：在空间里画出的边界，以及画线的动作。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN CAP: a rule or a fixed amount of money, time or water that may not be exceeded.
branches.cn: 写下来的上限：不可超过的规则，或金钱、时间、用水的定额。

branches.en: THE HONEST WEAKNESS: what a method cannot see, and the caveat that keeps a claim from spreading too far.
branches.cn: 诚实的弱点：方法看不到的东西，以及防止主张过度扩张的保留。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLOCK AND DEED: a period after which a right is barred, and a term fixed on an estate.
branches.cn: 法律的时钟与契据：过期即失权的期间，以及为地产设定的期限。

branches.en: THE LIABILITY CAP: the worst number named in advance so that risk can be borne.
branches.cn: 责任限额：事先写出的最坏数字，好让风险可以承担。

intro.en: Limitation is a Latin boundary word turned into an abstract noun, with a family that runs through law and science.
intro.cn: limitation 是把一个拉丁边界词变成抽象名词，其词族贯穿法律与科学。

latinIntro.en: Limes and limitare are the sources; the noun ending came through Latin limitatio.
latinIntro.cn: limes 与 limitare 是来源，名词词尾经由拉丁语 limitatio 而来。

items.meaning: a marking of bounds; a restriction
items.example: The noun covers a rule, a weakness and a legal period.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指规定、弱点与法定期间。

items.example: It named the edge of a field or of an empire.
items.exampleCN: 它指田地或帝国的边缘。

items.meaning: to bound, to mark a limit
items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供名词背后的动作。

items.example: It builds limitation, demarcation and estimation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成限制、划界与估计等词。

items.example: The short form is both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 短形既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: The participle became the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词成了日常形容词。

items.example: It builds limitless, the opposite of limited.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 limitless，即 limited 的反面。

items.example: It builds delimitation, the drawing of a border.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 delimitation，即划定边界。

items.example: It builds limiting, as in a limiting factor.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 limiting，如限制因素。

latinEntries.example: Latin limes means boundary or frontier.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 limes 意为边界、前线。

latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin limitare means to mark a boundary.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 limitare 意为划定边界。

latinEntries.example: Latin limitatio means a marking of bounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 limitatio 意为划定界限。

definition_zh: 无力的；软塌塌的；缺乏生气的；跛行；一瘸一拐地走；跛态
definition_en: lacking firmness or strength; to walk with a halting step; and a halting way of walking
core_image: 生菜叶在手里垂下来，梗再也撑不住叶片
scene: 菜市场收摊前，摊主把一袋放了一天的生菜拎起来，叶片软软地垂向地面。The lettuce had gone limp in the heat, so she sold it at half price.
sceneCN: 这里是「软塌塌的、失去挺括」（第 1 个义项：物体因失水或疲劳而变软）；句意为生菜在热气里变得软塌塌，她半价卖掉了。图中可辨识物件：塑料袋、垂下的叶片、菜摊的价牌。

pos.zh: 无力的；软塌塌的；缺乏生气的

derivatives.zh: 由 limp 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「无力地；软软地」
由 limp 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「柔软；无力」

senses.title: Soft and lacking firmness
senses.definition: soft and not firm, especially because of heat, tiredness or lack of water
senses.definitionCN: 柔软而不坚挺，尤因受热、疲乏或缺水
senses.example: The lettuce had gone limp in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 生菜在热气里变得软塌塌的。
senses.why: The adjective pictures something that can no longer hold its own weight, so the first sense is physical softness rather than moral weakness.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词的画面是某物再也撑不住自己的重量，所以第一层意思是物理上的软，而不是道德上的弱。

senses.title: Weak and lacking energy
senses.definition: without strength, force or energy, used of a handshake, a performance or a response
senses.definitionCN: 没有力气、力道或精神，用于握手、表现或回应
senses.example: His handshake was limp and brief.
senses.exampleCN: 他的握手无力而短促。
senses.why: A hand that does not grip is physically limp, and from that the word moves to anything that fails to show force.
senses.whyCN: 握手时手不使劲就是物理上的软，由此这个词扩展到任何显不出力道的东西。

senses.title: To walk with a halting step
senses.definition: to walk unevenly because one leg or foot hurts or cannot take full weight
senses.definitionCN: 因一条腿或脚疼痛、吃不住重量而走得高低不平
senses.example: He limped up the stairs with one hand on the rail.
senses.exampleCN: 他一只手扶着栏杆，一瘸一拐地上了楼。
senses.why: The walking verb probably began as a copy of the uneven rhythm itself, which is why the word sounds abrupt and short.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示走路的动词很可能起于对那种一高一低节奏的模仿，所以它读来短促而一顿一顿。

senses.title: A halting way of walking
senses.definition: a way of walking in which one leg moves unevenly, often caused by pain or injury
senses.definitionCN: 一条腿动作不均衡的走路方式，常由疼痛或受伤造成
senses.example: She still walks with a slight limp after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，她走路仍带一点跛态。
senses.why: The noun is the verb turned into a thing: the uneven gait itself becomes something a person has.
senses.whyCN: 名词是动词变成了一件东西：那种一高一低的步态本身，成了一个人身上带着的特征。

intro.en: Limp is a short, blunt word whose origin is uncertain, and it now covers softness, halting movement and the gait itself.
intro.cn: limp 是一个短促的词，来源不确定，如今同时覆盖柔软、跛行与跛态三件事。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the late fourteenth century, and no reliable Latin or Germanic source has been settled; some dictionaries suggest an unrecorded Old English verb of stumbling.
items.cn: 这个动词最早见于十四世纪晚期，可靠的拉丁语或日耳曼语来源尚无定论；一些词典推测它来自一个未被记录的、表示「踉跄」的古英语动词。

items.en: Middle English had limpen and limpien for walking badly, and the short form limp survived.
items.cn: 中古英语有 limpen、limpien 表示走路不稳，后来短形 limp 留存下来。

items.en: The noun a limp appears beside the verb, naming the uneven gait rather than the action of walking.
items.cn: 名词 a limp 与动词同时出现，指那种一高一低的步态，而不是走这个动作。

items.en: The adjective limp, meaning flaccid and unable to hold its shape, is recorded in the eighteenth century, and its link to the verb is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 limp 意为松软、撑不住形状，记录于十八世纪，它与动词的联系并不确定。

items.en: Modern English uses all three parts of speech and extends the adjective to weak handshakes, dull writing and tired vegetables.
items.cn: 现代英语三种词性都在使用，并把形容词扩展到无力的握手、乏味的文字和蔫掉的蔬菜。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers close spellings, including one Latin word that only looks related; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of moving badly or being weak.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词，其中有一个只是形似的拉丁词；近义组收其他表示「走得不稳」或「虚弱」的说法。

entries.definition: In a weak or soft way, without force.
entries.definitionCN: 无力地；软软地。

entries.definition: The quality of being soft or without strength.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软；无力。

entries.definition: Clear and transparent, from Latin limpidus; the spelling is close, but the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 清澈透明的，来自拉丁语 limpidus；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: Supple and bending easily; only the spelling suggests a link with this word.
entries.definitionCN: 柔韧易弯的；只有拼写暗示它与此词有联系。

entries.definition: To walk with short, awkward steps, often because of pain.
entries.definitionCN: 因疼痛而小步蹒跚地走。

entries.definition: To walk unsteadily as if about to fall.
entries.definitionCN: 摇晃不稳地走，像要摔倒。

entries.definition: To move or speak with hesitation and weakening strength.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或说话犹疑、力道渐弱。

entries.definition: Lacking strength or firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏力气或不够坚挺的。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and imitative, so the hooks come from the hanging leaf, the uneven step and the small family it has gathered.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短促而带有模仿性，所以记忆钩子来自垂下的叶片、一高一低的脚步，以及它聚起的小小词族。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb look identical, so only the sentence tells you whether limp means soft or lame.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词拼写完全相同，只有句子才能告诉你 limp 指「软」还是「跛」。

normal.en: Limp takes -ed and -ing regularly: limped and limping, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: limp 规则地加 -ed、-ing：limped、limping，词尾辅音不双写。

normal.en: Limply and limpness are the adverb and noun built on the adjective with -ly and -ness.
normal.cn: limply 与 limpness 是形容词加 -ly、-ness 构成的副词与名词。

normal.en: Go limp means to lose all tension at once, as a body does when it faints.
normal.cn: go limp 意为一下子失去全部张力，就像人昏过去时身体那样。

normal.en: Limp along means to keep going slowly and with difficulty, like a wounded walker.
normal.cn: limp along 意为像受伤的行人那样，缓慢而吃力地维持下去。

abstract.en: A leaf that cannot hold itself up and a leg that cannot take weight show the same failure of support.
abstract.cn: 撑不住自己的叶子和吃不住重量的腿，显出同一种支撑的失效。

abstract.en: The word refuses to say why: softness and lameness are simply two shapes of not holding firm.
abstract.cn: 这个词不肯说明原因：软与跛，不过都是「撑不住」的两种形状。

abstract.en: A short word with an uncertain past is a good reminder that not every sound can be traced home.
abstract.cn: 一个来历不确定的短词提醒人：并不是每个声音都能被追溯到家。

examples.en: The lettuce had gone limp in the heat.
examples.cn: 生菜在热气里变得软塌塌的。

examples.en: He limped up the stairs with one hand on the rail.
examples.cn: 他一只手扶着栏杆，一瘸一拐地上了楼。

examples.en: She still walks with a slight limp after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后，她走路仍带一点跛态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林普」——林子边一根普普通通的拐杖，撑着人一瘸一拐地走；limp 是跛行。

root: 来源不确定：动词 limp（跛行）最早见于十四世纪晚期，中古英语作 limpen、limpien；形容词 limp（松软）记录于十八世纪，一般认为与动词有某种联系，但没有可靠证据；无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is failing to hold firm; the senses divide into physical softness, lack of force, the halting action, and the gait as a thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「撑不住」；义项由此分为物体软塌、力道不足、跛行这个动作，以及作为名词的跛态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lettuce leaf drooping in the hand because its stem can no longer hold it up.
core.cn: 核心意象：生菜叶在手里垂下来，梗再也撑不住叶片。

branches.en: a leaf drooping over the edge of a bag
branches.cn: 垂在袋口的菜叶

branches.en: a hand that does not grip back
branches.cn: 没有回握的手

branches.en: a slow climb with one hand on the rail
branches.cn: 一手扶栏的缓慢上楼

branches.en: a slight unevenness in every step
branches.cn: 每一步里轻微的一高一低

branches.en: one body failing to hold its shape
branches.cn: 一具撑不住形状的身体

intro.en: The word has no prefix, so the entries are its Middle English source and the suffixes it takes in English.
intro.cn: 这个词没有前缀，因此条目是它的中古英语来源，以及它在英语中接受的几个后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 线；线条；排；队；线路；铁路线；一行字；台词
definition_en: a long thin mark drawn on a surface, a row of people or things, a route or railway track, a row of written words, or the words an actor speaks
core_image: 一根细线在纸面上被拉直，留下一道笔直的灰痕
scene: 雨停后，操场上还留着一条浅浅的白线，孩子们沿着它站成一排。The teacher told the class to stand in a line before the race.
sceneCN: 这里 line 是「排、队」（第 2 个义项：人排成的一列）；句意为老师让全班在比赛前排成一排。图中可辨识物件：浅浅的白线、塑胶跑道、站成一列的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 由 line 加 -ar 构成，义为「直线的；线性的」
经古法语 ligne 进入英语，义为「世系；血统」，指一脉相承的线
由 line 加 -ing 构成，义为「衬里；内层」，指贴在内侧的一层
由 line 与 up 复合，义为「阵容；排好的一队人」

senses.title: A long thin mark on a surface
senses.definition: a long narrow mark left on a surface, especially one drawn or printed straight
senses.definitionCN: 留在表面上的细长痕迹，尤指画得或印得笔直的痕迹
senses.example: Draw a straight line from the dot to the edge.
senses.exampleCN: 从那个点画一条直线到边缘。
senses.why: Latin linea first named a thread of linen, and a thread pulled tight is the oldest straight edge; the mark left on paper inherited the name of the thread.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 linea 本指一根亚麻线，而把线拉紧正是最古老的直边；纸上留下的痕迹便继承了这根线的名字。

senses.title: A row of people or things waiting
senses.definition: a row of people or things standing one behind another, especially while waiting for something
senses.definitionCN: 人或物一个接一个排成的一列，尤指等候某事时形成的队伍
senses.example: We stood in line for an hour to get tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 我们排了一个小时的队才买到票。
senses.why: A drawn line and a queue have the same outline, one long narrow strip; English lets the visible stripe stand for the people standing along it.
senses.whyCN: 画出的线和排队的人群轮廓相同，都是一条细长的带子；英语便让这条看得见的带子代替站在上面的人。

senses.title: A route or a track for transport
senses.definition: a route along which buses, trains or other transport run, or a set of rails laid for trains
senses.definitionCN: 公共汽车、火车等运行的路线，或为火车铺设的轨道
senses.example: The new line will connect the airport with the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新线路将把机场与市中心连接起来。
senses.why: A route becomes a line the moment it is drawn on a map, and transport planners still speak of opening a line; the map stroke turned into the thing travellers ride.
senses.whyCN: 一条路线画上地图的那一刻就成了「线」，交通规划者至今也说「开一条线」；地图上的一笔于是变成了乘客乘坐的东西。

senses.title: A row of written words
senses.definition: a row of written or printed words, especially one verse of a poem or one entry in a list
senses.definitionCN: 书写或印刷出来的一行字，尤指诗的一行或清单中的一项
senses.example: The first line of the poem is repeated at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的第一行在结尾处重复出现。
senses.why: Printing sets words in a narrow horizontal band, and that band repeats the shape of a drawn stroke; the row of type took over the same name.
senses.whyCN: 印刷把文字排进一条窄窄的水平带，这条带子和画出的一笔形状相同；于是一行铅字也用了同一个名字。

senses.title: Words spoken by an actor
senses.definition: one of the sentences that an actor has to speak in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 演员在戏剧或电影中要说的一句或几句词
senses.example: She forgot her line in the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第二幕忘了自己的台词。
senses.why: A script is set out row by row, each row assigned to a character; the written row became the actor's unit of speech, so the page's line turned into the stage's line.
senses.whyCN: 剧本是一行一行写成的，每一行分给一个角色；纸上的一行于是成了演员说话的单位，页面上的一行就变成了台上的一句台词。

intro.en: Line comes from a Latin word for a linen thread, and that thread is the physical model behind every later sense.
intro.cn: line 来自拉丁语中表示「亚麻线」的词，而这根线正是后来每个义项背后的实物模型。

items.en: Linum named the flax plant and the cloth woven from it; Greek linon is the older form of the same word.
items.cn: linum 指亚麻这种植物，也指用它织成的布；希腊语 linon 是同一个词更早的形式。

items.en: A linea was a thread of linen and then any cord; stretched between two points, it also marked a boundary or a straight edge.
items.cn: linea 本是一根亚麻线，后来泛指绳子；在两点之间拉紧时，它还能标出边界或直边。

items.en: The verb lineare meant to make something straight or to set it in a line, and linearis described whatever belongs to a line.
items.cn: 动词 lineare 意为使某物变直或排成一线，形容词 linearis 则描述与线有关的东西。

items.en: Old French ligne carried the senses of a line, a row and a line of descent, and English borrowed it after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语的 ligne 兼指线、行以及一脉相承的世系，英语在诺曼时期之后把它借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the drawn mark and adds the queue, the railway route, the verse row, the actor's speech and a whole field of work.
items.cn: 现代英语保留画出的痕迹，又加上队列、铁路线路、诗行、演员的台词，以及某一个行业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin thread of linen; the near-meaning group gathers words for rows, routes and borders.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「亚麻线」之上的词；近义组收表示行、路线与边界的词。

entries.definition: To put things into a straight line, from French a ligne, literally into line.
entries.definitionCN: 使排成直线；来自法语 a ligne，字面就是「成线」，与 line 同源。

entries.definition: A line of descent from an ancestor.
entries.definitionCN: 世系；血统；沿用古法语 ligne 中「一脉相承的线」这一用法。

entries.definition: Arranged in a line or relating to lines.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线的；与线有关的；由 line 加 -ar 构成。

entries.definition: Cloth woven from flax.
entries.definitionCN: 亚麻布；与 line 同出拉丁语 linum（亚麻）。

entries.definition: A number of things arranged side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 一排；一行，横向并排的一列东西。

entries.definition: A line of people waiting for something, the usual British word.
entries.definitionCN: 排队等候的队伍，英式常用说法。

entries.definition: The way from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 路线；从一处到另一处的路径。

entries.definition: The line that marks the edge of an area.
entries.definitionCN: 边界；标出一个区域边缘的线。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a thread of linen, and every branch keeps the shape of one long narrow strip.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一根亚麻线，后来每个分支都保留着一条细长带子的形状。

normal.en: Latin linea is a linen thread and linum is the flax plant that makes it, so the word is a string before it is a mark.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 linea 是一根亚麻线，linum 是织出它的亚麻；所以这个词先是绳子，后来才是痕迹。

normal.en: A mason stretches a cord between two pegs to keep a wall straight, which is why a drawn mark and a boundary share one word.
normal.cn: 泥瓦匠在两个木桩之间拉紧一根绳来把墙砌直，画出的痕迹与边界因此共用一个词。

normal.en: On a map every railway is a single stroke, so a company calls its route a line.
normal.cn: 在地图上每条铁路都是一笔，所以铁路公司把自己的路线叫作 line。

normal.en: A poem is printed in rows, and an actor is handed one row at a time; the written row and the spoken line are the same shape.
normal.cn: 诗是一行一行印出来的，演员也一次拿到一行；纸上的一行和口中的一句形状相同。

normal.en: Americans stand in line while the British stand in a queue; both describe one narrow strip of waiting people.
normal.cn: 美国人说 stand in line，英国人说 stand in a queue，两种说法都是在描述一条细长的等候队伍。

abstract.en: One word for thread, mark, queue, rail and speech suggests English trusts a single shape to hold very different things.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示线、痕迹、队列、铁轨和台词，说明英语相信一种形状就能装下很不一样的东西。

abstract.en: A line both joins and separates: it connects two points and it divides two fields.
abstract.cn: 线既能连接也能分隔：它把两点连起来，也把两片田地分开。

abstract.en: Reading a script row by row is a reminder that a play exists first as lines on paper.
abstract.cn: 一行一行读剧本会让人想起：一出戏最初只是纸上的一行行字。

examples.en: Draw a straight line from the dot to the edge.
examples.cn: 从那个点画一条直线到边缘。

examples.en: We stood in line for an hour to get tickets.
examples.cn: 我们排了一个小时的队才买到票。

examples.en: She forgot her line in the second act.
examples.cn: 她在第二幕忘了自己的台词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来印」——把一根线拉直了在纸上印一下，就留下笔直的一道；line 是线，也是排队的一条线。

root: 拉丁语 linum（亚麻）→ linea（亚麻线、线、界线）→ 古法语 ligne → 英语 line；同族词多与线、排列、连续的血脉有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a taut thread; from it flow the drawn mark, the queue, the route on a map, the printed row and the actor's speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一根拉紧的线；由此分出画出的痕迹、排队的人群、地图上的路线、印刷的一行字和演员的台词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut thread laid across paper, leaving one straight grey mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根拉紧的线横过纸面，留下一道笔直的灰痕。

branches.en: a pencil drawing a ruled line across the page
branches.cn: 铅笔在纸上画出一道笔直的线

branches.en: a map with one long stroke joining two towns
branches.cn: 地图上一条长线连起两个城镇

branches.en: a queue curling past the ticket window
branches.cn: 排队的人绕过了售票窗口

branches.en: a poem printed in even rows
branches.cn: 一首诗排成整齐的诗行

branches.en: an actor waiting for a cue backstage
branches.cn: 演员在后台等提示

intro.en: A Latin word for flax, its thread and its verb, a French reshaping and two English suffixes carry line from string to mark, route and speech.
intro.cn: 一个表示亚麻的拉丁词、它的「线」和动词形式、一次法语改写，再加两个英语后缀，把 line 从绳子一路带到痕迹、路线与台词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 链环；连接物；纽带；连接；关联；链接
definition_en: one ring of a chain; something that joins two things; to connect or associate people, objects, or ideas
core_image: 两段铁链由中间一个环扣住，环环相扣，力量沿链条传递
scene: 铁路调度室里，调度员把两个货运站接进同一条新支线。He used the panel to link the two freight yards to the new branch line, and a green line appeared between the two dots.
sceneCN: 这里 link 是「把两点连成一条线路」（第 6 个义项：交通连线）；句意：他用调度台把两个货运站连到新支线上，屏幕上两点之间多出一条绿线。图中可辨识物件：铁路线路图、两个货运站标记、新支线绿线、调度台；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.phrase: a link between A and B
collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的联系
把 A 连接到 B

derivatives.zh: 连接；联系；联动机制
相连的；有关联的
连接程序；链接器
连接；会合；联合

senses.title: Chain ring: one loop in a chain
senses.definition: a single ring of metal that forms one unit of a chain
senses.definitionCN: 构成链条一个单元的单个金属环
senses.example: One link of the chain had rusted through.
senses.exampleCN: 链条上有一个环已经锈穿了。
senses.why: The earliest English sense is the physical ring. Everything else grows from this object: a chain is a row of rings, and each ring holds the next.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项就是这种实体环。其余义项都从这一物件生长出来：链条是一排环，而每个环都扣住下一个。

senses.title: Connector: a piece that joins two ends
senses.titleCN: 连接件：把两端扣在一起的部件
senses.definition: a physical part or device that fastens two separate parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个分离部件扣合在一起的实体部件或装置
senses.example: A steel link joined the two sections of the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 一个钢制连接件把围栏的两段接了起来。
senses.why: A chain ring already does the work of holding two neighbours. The word is therefore ready to name any small piece whose job is to join two ends.
senses.whyCN: 链环本来就在承担“扣住左右两环”的工作。因此这个词很自然地可以指任何以“接合两端”为职责的小部件。

senses.title: Bond between people or groups
senses.titleCN: 纽带：人与人、群体与群体之间的联结
senses.definition: a relationship or connection between people, groups, or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 人与人、群体或组织之间的关系或联结
senses.example: The exchange programme created a lasting link between the two schools.
senses.exampleCN: 交换项目在两所学校之间建立了持久的纽带。
senses.why: Move from metal to society: the ring that held two chain ends now holds two people or institutions. The connection is no longer visible, but it still constrains and carries.
senses.whyCN: 从金属转向社会：原本扣住两节链子的环，现在扣住两个人或两个机构。联结不再可见，但仍在约束与传递。

senses.title: Join physically: connect two things
senses.titleCN: 实体连接：把两件东西接起来
senses.definition: to connect two objects or places so that they are joined or can work together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个物体或地点连接起来，使其接合或能协同运作
senses.example: Workers linked the new pipe to the old water main.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把新管道接到旧的总水管上。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to link is to act as the ring, putting oneself or a part between two ends and holding them together.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：link 就是充当那个环，把自己或某个部件放在两端之间，把它们扣住。

senses.title: Associate ideas or evidence
senses.titleCN: 关联：把观念、证据或因果串起来
senses.definition: to show or establish a connection between ideas, facts, or causes
senses.definitionCN: 表明或建立观念、事实或原因之间的联系
senses.example: The study links long commutes to higher stress levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把长途通勤与更高的压力水平联系起来。
senses.why: A chain of reasoning is also a row of rings: each claim holds the next. To link two facts is to insert the ring that makes them one sequence rather than two isolated items.
senses.whyCN: 推理链同样是一排环：每个论断扣住下一个。把两个事实 link 起来，就是插入那个让它们成为一条序列、而非两个孤立项的环。

senses.title: Transport connection: a route between two points
senses.titleCN: 交通连线：连接两点的线路
senses.definition: a transport route or service that connects two places
senses.definitionCN: 连接两地的交通路线或运输服务
senses.example: The new rail link cuts the journey to forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 新的铁路连线把行程缩短到四十分钟。
senses.why: Two stations are like two chain ends; the rail line is the ring that joins them into one network. The image scales from a hand-held chain to a map.
senses.whyCN: 两个车站就像链条的两端，铁路线则是把二者接入同一网络的环。这个意象从手中的链条放大到地图上。

senses.title: Digital link: hyperlink or network connection
senses.titleCN: 数字链接：超链接或网络连接
senses.definition: a hyperlink in a document, or a connection between computers or network nodes
senses.definitionCN: 文档中的超链接，或计算机、网络节点之间的连接
senses.example: Click the link to open the full report.
senses.exampleCN: 点击链接打开完整报告。
senses.why: A webpage is a node and a hyperlink is the ring that carries a reader from one page to another. The same join-and-carry structure is now made of protocol rather than metal.
senses.whyCN: 网页是一个节点，超链接则是把读者从一页带到另一页的环。同样的“接合与传递”结构，如今由协议而不是金属构成。

senses.title: Link arms: join bodies in contact
senses.definition: to join arms or hands with someone, especially as a sign of closeness or support
senses.definitionCN: 与某人挽臂或牵手，尤表示亲近或相互支持
senses.example: The two friends linked arms and walked into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 两个朋友挽着手臂走进大厅。
senses.why: Here the human body supplies both ends: bent arms form the rings. The verb returns to its most concrete physical action while keeping the idea of mutual holding.
senses.whyCN: 这里两端都由人体提供：弯起的手臂就是环。动词回到最具体的身体动作，同时保留“相互扣住”的意思。

senses.title: Missing link: the absent ring in a sequence
senses.titleCN: 缺环：序列中缺失的一环
senses.definition: in the phrase missing link, the absent piece needed to complete an evolutionary or logical chain
senses.definitionCN: 用于 missing link，指完成演化链或论证链所缺的那一环
senses.example: The fossil was hailed as the missing link between the two species.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石被誉为两个物种之间缺失的一环。
senses.why: If a chain is only as strong as its rings, one absent ring breaks the sequence. The phrase turns a physical gap into a metaphor for an unexplained step.
senses.whyCN: 如果链条的强度取决于每一环，那么缺一个环就断了整条序列。这个短语把实体缺口变成了“无法解释的中间步骤”的隐喻。

senses.title: Link up: separate parts meet and join
senses.titleCN: 汇合：分开的部分相遇并联结
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb link up, to join or meet after being separate
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语动词 link up，表示原本分开的部分连接或会合
senses.example: The two rescue teams linked up at the tunnel entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 两支救援队在隧道口会合了。
senses.why: The particle up adds completion: the ring is not merely placed but closed. Separate parties become one continuous chain, which is why the phrase suits meetings and mergers.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 up 补充“完成”：环不只是放上去，而是扣合封闭。分开的各方变成一条连续的链，因此这个短语适合会合与合并。

intro.en: Link was borrowed from Old Norse, not inherited from Old English. The chain-ring sense is solid; the jump to a bend root in Indo-European is generally believed rather than proved.
intro.cn: link 是从古诺斯语借入的，而不是从古英语继承的。链环义很确定；上溯到印欧语“弯曲”词根则属于一般认为是，而非已经证明。

items.en: The noun probably comes from Old Norse hlekkr 'link of a chain', with a related verb hlekkja 'to chain'. Old Norse gave English many everyday words during the Viking period.
items.cn: 名词很可能来自古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，并有相关动词 hlekkja“用链子拴住”。维京时期古诺斯语给英语带来了大量日常词。

items.en: The Norse word is traced to Proto-Germanic *hlankiz, a formation from a root meaning 'to bend'. A ring is metal bent back on itself.
items.cn: 这个诺斯语词可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz，由表示“弯曲”的词根构成。环就是金属弯回自身形成的形状。

items.en: The deeper source is generally believed to be PIE *kleng- 'to bend, turn'. The same family is often linked to angle and other bend words, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 更深的来源一般认为是原始印欧语 *kleng-“弯曲、转折”。同一词族常被与 angle 等“弯折”词联系起来，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: English records the noun in the early 15c. and the verb in the late 14c., first in the literal sense of fitting with chain links.
items.cn: 英语中名词最早记录于 15 世纪早期，动词记录于 14 世纪晚期，最初都是“装上链环”的字面义。

items.en: From a metal ring the word extends to any connection: rail links, personal links, links between facts, and finally hyperlinks. The chain image survives in missing link and weakest link.
items.cn: 从金属环出发，这个词扩展到任何连接：铁路连线、人际纽带、事实之间的关联，最后是超链接。链条意象仍活在 missing link 与 weakest link 中。

note.en: The first group tests spelling and derivation around link; the second separates four kinds of connection by strength, direction, and domain.
note.cn: 第一组检查 link 周围的拼写与派生关系；第二组按强度、方向和领域区分四种“连接”。

entries.definition: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection. It is link plus the noun suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 连接行为或连接系统；机械或遗传上的联动。它是 link 加名词后缀 -age。

entries.definition: to shut and open the eyes quickly. It rhymes and looks close but has a different, uncertain origin.
entries.definitionCN: 快速眨眼。它押韵、词形接近，但来源不同且不确定。

entries.definition: coloured liquid used for writing or printing. It shares the -ink ending only; there is no link in it.
entries.definitionCN: 用于书写或印刷的彩色液体。它只共享 -ink 结尾，与 link 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: to join two things so that they touch or work together. It is the broad neutral verb, while link often suggests a chain-like intermediate part.
entries.definitionCN: 把两物接合，使其接触或协同运作。它是最宽泛中性的动词，而 link 常暗示有一个链环式的中间部件。

entries.definition: to fasten one thing to another, usually a smaller thing to a larger one. It stresses physical fixing, not mutual relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物固定到另一物上，通常是小物附于大物。它强调实体固定，而不是相互关联。

entries.definition: to tie or fasten tightly, or to place under a moral or legal obligation. It is stronger and more restrictive than link.
entries.definitionCN: 紧紧捆扎或固定，或使承担道德、法律义务。它比 link 更强、更具约束力。

entries.definition: the way two people or groups are connected and behave toward each other. It names the durable social tie that link describes.
entries.definitionCN: 两个人或群体相互连接与相处的方式。它命名了 link 所描述的那种持久社会纽带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the physical chain ring, the fixed phrases missing link and weakest link, and the modern hyperlink.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：实体的链环、固定短语 missing link 与 weakest link，以及现代的超链接。

normal.en: A chain is a row of rings; one ring is a link. Take one out and the chain falls apart.
normal.cn: 链条是一排环，一个环就是一个 link。取走一个，整条链就散了。

normal.en: The weakest link is the ring that breaks first, so the phrase means the most vulnerable part of any system.
normal.cn: weakest link 是最先断的那个环，因此这个短语指任何系统中最脆弱的部分。

normal.en: The missing link is the ring absent from a sequence, especially an evolutionary chain.
normal.cn: missing link 是序列中缺失的那个环，尤指演化链上的缺环。

normal.en: Link up means the ring is finally closed: two separate parties meet and become one chain.
normal.cn: link up 表示环终于扣合：两个分开的方会合，变成一条链。

normal.en: A hyperlink does the same job on the web: one click carries you from one page to the next.
normal.cn: 超链接在网络上做同一件事：一次点击把你从一页带到下一页。

abstract.en: Two islands with a bridge between them: the bridge is not either island, yet without it they are separate worlds.
abstract.cn: 两座岛之间有一座桥：桥不属于任何一座岛，但没有它，两座岛就是分开的世界。

abstract.en: A chain has no centre: every ring holds the next and is held by the previous, so the link is a position rather than a thing.
abstract.cn: 链条没有中心：每个环都扣住下一个，又被上一个扣住，因此“环”是一种位置，而不是一个孤立物件。

abstract.en: A web of nodes and edges: the nodes are what we see, the links are the invisible lines along which influence travels.
abstract.cn: 由节点和边构成的网：节点是我们看得见的东西，链接则是影响沿之传递的看不见的线。

examples.en: The bridge links the island to the mainland.
examples.cn: 这座桥把海岛与大陆连接起来。

examples.en: Researchers have found a link between sleep loss and poor memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠不足与记忆力差之间存在关联。

examples.en: Send me the link to the recording when it is ready.
examples.cn: 录音准备好后把链接发给我。

dict_mnemonic.text: “林克”——游戏主角林克把地图上的各个地点串起来 → link 连接

root: 古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz；核心是“一环扣一环”，引申为任何连接、纽带与关联。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of link, all built on one object: a ring that holds two ends together. The ring becomes a connector, a human bond, a route, a hyperlink, a missing step, and finally the act of closing the chain.
sensesIntro.cn: link 的十个义项都建立在一个物件上：把两端扣住的环。这个环变成连接件、人际纽带、线路、超链接、缺失的步骤，最后变成“把链扣合”的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ring holds the ring before it and the ring after it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个环同时扣住前一个环与后一个环。

branches.en: PHYSICAL RING: the literal chain link and any part that fastens two ends.
branches.cn: 实体环：字面的链环，以及任何接合两端的部件。

branches.en: HUMAN CONTACT: the ring becomes a bond between people or a joining of arms.
branches.cn: 人际接触：环变成人与人之间的纽带，或手臂的相互扣住。

branches.en: INFRASTRUCTURE: pipes, rails and routes are rings that join places into a network.
branches.cn: 基础设施：管道、铁路与航线都是把地点接入网络的环。

branches.en: LOGICAL CHAIN: facts are linked like rings, and a missing ring explains why a sequence fails.
branches.cn: 逻辑链：事实像环一样被串起，缺环则解释了序列为何断裂。

branches.en: DIGITAL AND COMPLETION: a hyperlink carries a reader, and link up closes the ring.
branches.cn: 数字与完成：超链接把读者带过去，link up 则把环扣合封闭。

intro.en: Link is a borrowed Germanic noun and verb, not a prefixed Latin word. English adds -age, -ed, -er and -ing to build its family.
intro.cn: link 是借入的日耳曼语名词兼动词，不是带前缀的拉丁词。英语通过 -age、-ed、-er、-ing 构成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Link has no Latin ancestor. If the Indo-European bend root *kleng- is correct, it is a distant cousin of angle, ankle and anchor, but that link is generally believed rather than established.
latinIntro.cn: link 没有拉丁语祖先。如果印欧语“弯曲”词根 *kleng- 成立，它与 angle、ankle、anchor 是远亲，但这一联系只是一般认为，并未确立。

items.meaning: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection
items.meaningCN: 连接；联系；联动机制（-age 构成行为或系统名词）
items.example: The linkage between the two levers controls the brake.
items.exampleCN: 两根杠杆之间的联动机构控制刹车。

items.meaningCN: 相连的；有关联的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The two problems are closely linked.

items.meaning: a program or device that joins separate pieces
items.meaningCN: 连接程序；链接器（-er 表示执行该动作的物）
items.example: The linker combines the object files into one program.
items.exampleCN: 链接器把多个目标文件合并成一个程序。

items.meaning: the act of connecting; serving to connect
items.meaningCN: 连接；起连接作用的（-ing 构成动作或功能词）
items.example: A linking verb joins a subject to its description.
items.exampleCN: 连系动词把主语与其描述连接起来。

items.example: It forms linkage, a set of connections.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 linkage，即一组连接。

items.example: You can unlink the file from the message.
items.exampleCN: 你可以把文件从消息里解除链接。

items.meaning: a clickable cross-reference on a page
items.example: Click the hyperlink to open the source.

items.meaning: a joining of two systems or groups
items.example: The rail link-up took ten years to complete.
items.exampleCN: 这条铁路的接轨花了十年才完成。

latinEntries.meaning: a corner or the space between two lines
latinEntries.meaningCN: 角；两条线之间的空间（与“弯曲”词根有远亲关系）

latinEntries.structure: Old English ancleow, from PIE *ang- (to bend)
latinEntries.meaning: the joint where the foot bends
a heavy device that holds a ship in place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 锚；把船固定住的重物（原义与“弯钩”有关）
三角形；有三个角的平面图形

definition_zh: 嘴唇；边缘；口沿；不逊的话；（兰花的）唇瓣
definition_en: either of the two soft edges of the mouth, the rim of an opening, rude talk, or the lower petal of an orchid
core_image: 两片柔软的唇轻轻合拢，嘴角压成一条浅浅的缝
scene: 冬天的风把孩子的嘴唇吹得发红，他忍不住舔了舔。The cold wind left her lips dry and cracked.
sceneCN: 这里 lip 是「嘴唇」（第 1 个义项：嘴的两片软边）；句意为冷风把她的嘴唇吹得又干又裂。图中可辨识物件：冻红的脸、干裂的嘴角、竖起的衣领。

pos.zh: 嘴唇；边缘；口沿；不逊的话；（兰花的）唇瓣

derivatives.zh: 由 lip 加 -y 构成，义为「爱顶嘴的；无礼的」，多用于英式口语
由 lip 与 stick 复合，义为「口红」
由 lip 与 read 复合，义为「看口型读懂话」
由 lip 与 sync 复合，义为「对口型假唱」

senses.title: Either of the two soft edges of the mouth
senses.definition: either of the two soft, movable edges that close the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 闭合嘴部的两片柔软、可活动的边缘
senses.example: He pressed his lips together and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他抿紧嘴唇，什么也没说。
senses.why: Old English lippa named the fleshy edge of the mouth, and that body part is still the word's centre; every later sense is cut to its outline.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lippa 指的就是嘴边的肉，这个身体部位至今仍是词的核心；后来每个义项都是照着它的轮廓剪出来的。

senses.title: The rim of a container or opening
senses.definition: the edge or rim of a container, hole or opening, especially one that curves outward
senses.definitionCN: 容器、洞口或开口的边缘，尤指略微向外翻的口沿
senses.example: She wiped the lip of the cup before pouring.
senses.exampleCN: 倒水之前她擦了擦杯口。
senses.why: A mouth is a soft edge around an opening, and a cup or a crater has the same outline; English borrows the body word for any raised rim.
senses.whyCN: 嘴是围在开口周围的一圈软边，杯子和火山口也有同样的轮廓；英语便借这个身体词来指任何凸起的边沿。

senses.title: Rude or disrespectful talk
senses.definition: rude or disrespectful remarks, especially when a younger person answers back
senses.definitionCN: 无礼、不敬的话，尤指晚辈对长辈顶嘴
senses.example: Don't give me any lip about the chores.
senses.exampleCN: 别为了家务跟我顶嘴。
senses.why: Speech comes out of the mouth, and the lip is the visible gate of the mouth; insolent words are pictured as something pushed through that gate.
senses.whyCN: 话从嘴里出来，嘴唇就是嘴看得见的门；无礼的话被想成硬从这扇门里推出来的东西。

senses.title: The lower petal of an orchid
senses.definition: the lower petal of an orchid, which is usually larger and differently shaped
senses.definitionCN: 兰花下方那片通常更大、形状也不同的花瓣
senses.example: The orchid's lip is marked with dark purple spots.
senses.exampleCN: 这朵兰花下方的唇瓣上带着深紫色的斑点。
senses.why: Botanists needed a name for the petal that hangs out like a lower lip, and the everyday body word was ready at hand.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家需要给那片像下唇一样探出来的花瓣起名，手边现成的身体词正好可用。

intro.en: Lip is an Old English word for the edge of the mouth; its Germanic relatives are close, but the path further back is uncertain.
intro.cn: lip 是古英语中表示「嘴的边缘」的词；它在日耳曼语族中的亲属很近，但再往前追溯则来源不确定。

items.en: Old English records lippa for the edge of the mouth, a weak noun that already meant the body part.
items.cn: 古英语用 lippa 指嘴的边缘，这是个弱变化名词，当时已经专指这个身体部位。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family with Dutch lip and German Lippe; the reconstructed ancestor is usually written with a doubled consonant, though its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词属于一个日耳曼语族，与荷兰语 lip、德语 Lippe 同族；重构的祖形通常写作带双辅音的形式，但确切形态不确定。

items.en: Beyond Germanic the origin is uncertain; a link with Latin labium has been suggested but is not reliably established.
items.cn: 再往上追溯来源不确定；有人提出它与拉丁语 labium 有关，但并未可靠证实。

items.en: Middle English lippe continues the bodily sense and settles the modern spelling without adding new meanings.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lippe 延续了身体部位的义项，并稳定了现代拼写，没有增加新的意思。

items.en: Modern English extends lip to the rim of vessels, to insolent speech, and to the lip-shaped petal of an orchid.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lip 扩展到器皿的口沿、无礼的言语，以及兰花的唇状花瓣。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on lip plus one Latin word for a lip; the near-meaning group collects words for mouths and edges.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lip 构成的复合词、派生词，以及一个意为「唇」的拉丁词；近义组收表示嘴与边缘的词。

entries.definition: Coloured cosmetic for the lips.
entries.definitionCN: 口红；由 lip 与 stick 复合而成。

entries.definition: Inclined to answer back rudely.
entries.definitionCN: 爱顶嘴的；由 lip 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: To understand speech by watching the speaker's lips.
entries.definitionCN: 看口型读懂话；由 lip 与 read 复合。

entries.definition: A Latin word for a lip, also used in anatomy for a lip-like fold.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「唇」的词，解剖学也用来指唇状褶；它与 lip 只是意义相近，拼写与词源都不同。

entries.definition: The whole opening in the face used for eating and speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 嘴；脸上用来进食和说话的整个开口，lip 只是它的一部分。

entries.definition: The outer edge of a round or curved object.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形或弧形物体的外缘。

entries.definition: The outside limit of an object or area.
entries.definitionCN: 物体或区域的边缘。

entries.definition: The top edge of a cup or the projecting edge of a hat.
entries.definitionCN: 杯口的上沿；帽檐。

normalIntro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun for the edge of the mouth, and its family keeps returning to soft rims and openings.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，指嘴的边缘；它的同族词反复回到柔软的边沿与开口。

normal.en: Old English lippa already meant the edge of the mouth, so the body part is the oldest sense and the others borrow its outline.
normal.cn: 古英语 lippa 已经指嘴的边缘，所以身体部位是最早的义项，其他义项都借用了它的轮廓。

normal.en: Dutch lip and German Lippe are close cousins, and the short word has stayed almost unchanged around the North Sea.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 lip 和德语 Lippe 是近亲，这个短词在北海两岸几乎原样保留了下来。

normal.en: Lipstick puts lip in front of stick, and the compound never loses the mouth at its centre.
normal.cn: lipstick 把 lip 放在 stick 前面，这个复合词始终没有丢掉中心那个「嘴」。

normal.en: A cup has a lip because a cup and a mouth are both soft edges around an opening.
normal.cn: 杯子有 lip，是因为杯子和嘴都是围在开口周围的一圈软边。

normal.en: To give someone lip is to push rude words through the same gate that lets food in.
normal.cn: 对某人 give lip，就是把无礼的话从同一扇也放食物进来的门里推出去。

abstract.en: A lip is a border that can open, which makes it a fitting image for the edge of anything that must let something through.
abstract.cn: 嘴唇是一道能开的边界，很适合用来比喻任何必须放东西通过的边缘。

abstract.en: The same word covers a mouth, a cup and a crater because all three are openings with a raised rim.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖嘴、杯子和火山口，因为这三者都是带凸起边沿的开口。

abstract.en: Silence is often described as pressed lips, a reminder that the mouth's edge can shut as well as speak.
abstract.cn: 沉默常被写成抿紧的双唇，这提醒人：嘴的边缘既能说话，也能关上。

examples.en: He pressed his lips together and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他抿紧嘴唇，什么也没说。

examples.en: She wiped the lip of the cup before pouring.
examples.cn: 倒水之前她擦了擦杯口。

examples.en: The orchid's lip is marked with dark purple spots.
examples.cn: 这朵兰花下方的唇瓣上带着深紫色的斑点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里普」——他顶着嘴说个不停，靠的就是这张嘴；lip 是嘴唇，也是杯口那道边。

root: 古英语 lippa（嘴唇）；与荷兰语 lip、德语 Lippe 同属一个日耳曼语族。更早的来源不确定，与拉丁语 labium（唇）的关系未获可靠证实。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the soft edge of the mouth; from it come the rim of any opening, the insolent words pushed through that gate, and the orchid petal shaped like a lip.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是嘴边的软边；由此分出任何开口的边沿、从这扇门推出去的无礼话，以及形状像唇的兰花花瓣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two soft lips pressed together, closing an opening at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：两片柔软的嘴唇合在一起，在开口的边缘把它关上。

branches.en: two lips meeting in a quiet line
branches.cn: 两片嘴唇轻轻合拢成一条线

branches.en: a child answering back with a pout
branches.cn: 孩子嘟着嘴顶了一句

branches.en: a jug tipped at its rim
branches.cn: 壶口倾斜，水从边沿流出

branches.en: a flower whose lowest petal hangs like a lip
branches.cn: 一朵花最低的花瓣垂下来像一片唇

branches.en: words pushing out through the mouth
branches.cn: 话从嘴里推了出来

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun for the mouth's edge, and English builds compounds and a suffix on that base without adding a prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，指嘴的边缘；英语在这个词基上造复合词、加后缀，却没有加前缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin labium means lip, but the resemblance has not been shown to rest on a shared root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 labium 意为「唇」，但相似之处尚未被证明来自共同词根。

definition_zh: 液体的；液态的；流动而清澈的；（资产）易变现的；现金充裕的
definition_en: in the state of a substance that flows freely, clear and smooth, or easily converted into cash
core_image: 一只玻璃杯里水沿杯壁滑下，杯底的硬币清晰可见
scene: 孩子把杯子打翻，水沿着桌沿流下，滴在地板上。The child knocked the cup over and the liquid ran along the table edge onto the floor.
sceneCN: 这里指「能自由流动的液体」（第 1 个义项：有一定体积而无固定形状、可流动的物质状态）；句意为孩子打翻杯子，液体沿桌沿流下，滴到地板上。可辨识物件：玻璃杯、桌沿、水滴、地板；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 液体的；液态的；清澈流动的；（资产）易变现的

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词加名词后缀，表性质 → 流动性
基础词干加使动后缀 → 使液化
由该动词加名词后缀 → 液化
